questions.stem: A biochemist describes a hepatic process in which individual amino acids are joined by peptide bonds at the ribosome to synthesize a new protein, a process that consumes a large fraction of the cell's ATP. This process is best classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A catabolic, energy-releasing process

choices.label: B
choices.text: A process that is neither anabolic nor catabolic

choices.label: C
choices.text: An anabolic, energy-consuming process

choices.label: D
choices.text: An oxidative process that generates ATP

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glycogenolysis

explanation.summary: Building larger molecules from smaller ones while consuming energy is anabolism.
explanation.whyCorrect: Anabolism is the building up of smaller molecules into larger ones in an energy-dependent process. Synthesis of a protein from amino acids at the ribosome by forming peptide bonds is anabolic and is a predominant source of ATP expenditure within a cell.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Catabolism breaks complex molecules down into smaller ones and releases energy; protein synthesis does the opposite.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Protein synthesis is a clear example of anabolism, so it can be classified.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The process consumes ATP rather than generating it, and it is a reductive/anabolic build-up, not an ATP-yielding oxidation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glycogenolysis is the catabolic breakdown of glycogen to glucose and is unrelated to protein synthesis.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: The amino acid tyrosine is synthesized from the amino acid phenylalanine. Considering only the perspective of phenylalanine, the transformation is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anabolic, because a new amino acid is formed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Catabolic, because ATP is always produced when phenylalanine reacts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Catabolic, because phenylalanine is consumed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Energy-independent, because no ATP is involved

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neither anabolic nor catabolic, because amino acids cannot be interconverted

explanation.summary: The same reaction can be catabolic or anabolic depending on which molecule's perspective is taken.
explanation.whyCorrect: From the perspective of phenylalanine, the reaction is catabolic because phenylalanine is consumed. From the perspective of tyrosine the same reaction is anabolic because tyrosine is produced, illustrating why perspective matters when classifying pathways.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Forming tyrosine is anabolic only from tyrosine's perspective; the question specifies phenylalanine's perspective, from which it is catabolic.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ATP is not always produced when phenylalanine reacts, and that is not the reason this is catabolic from phenylalanine's viewpoint.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Whether ATP is involved is not the basis for calling it catabolic; consumption of phenylalanine defines it as catabolic here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phenylalanine is in fact converted to tyrosine, so the transformation can be classified.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Using the metabolic definitions of oxidation and reduction, which of the following molecular changes constitutes an oxidation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gain of a bond to hydrogen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gain of a bond to oxygen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of a bond to nitrogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of a bond to oxygen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of a bond to sulfur

explanation.summary: Oxidation is the gain of bonds to oxygen, nitrogen, or sulfur and/or the loss of bonds to hydrogen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gaining a bond to oxygen fits the definition of oxidation, which is the gain of bonds to oxygen, nitrogen, or sulfur and/or the loss of bonds to hydrogen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gaining a bond to hydrogen is a reduction, the opposite of oxidation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Losing a bond to nitrogen is a reduction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Losing a bond to oxygen is a reduction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Losing a bond to sulfur is a reduction.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Alcohol dehydrogenase oxidizes retinol (vitamin A) to retinaldehyde. Because oxidation and reduction reactions occur in concert, what happens to the NAD+ coenzyme during this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is oxidized to NADH

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is phosphorylated to NADP+

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is reduced to FADH2

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is reduced to NADH

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is unchanged because electrons pass directly to oxygen

explanation.summary: When a biomolecule is oxidized, its partner coenzyme is concomitantly reduced.
explanation.whyCorrect: A reactant can only be oxidized if another is reduced. As vitamin A is oxidized to retinaldehyde, the NAD+ coenzyme is concomitantly reduced to NADH, acting as the electron shuttle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: NAD+ to NADH is a reduction; NADH is the reduced form of the coenzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Phosphorylation of NAD+ to NADP+ is not part of this oxidoreductase reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FADH2 is the reduced form of FAD, a different coenzyme not used by alcohol dehydrogenase here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The electrons are captured by NAD+ to form NADH, not passed directly to oxygen in this step.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Vitamin A (retinol) is a largely inert nutrient that is sequentially oxidized by alcohol dehydrogenase and then aldehyde dehydrogenase. The final product, retinoic acid, is most important for which of the following functions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Embryonic development, tissue maintenance, and immunity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maintaining blood glucose during prolonged overnight fasting

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serving as the terminal electron acceptor of the electron transport chain

choices.label: D
choices.text: Substrate-level ATP production during anaerobic glycolysis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vision, by combining with opsin to form rhodopsin in rods

explanation.summary: Oxidative biotransformation converts inert retinol into bioactive derivatives with distinct roles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Retinoic acid, the fully oxidized carboxylic acid product, is critical for embryonic development, tissue maintenance, and immunity.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blood glucose during fasting is maintained by glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, not retinoic acid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxygen, not retinoic acid, is the terminal electron acceptor in the electron transport chain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Retinoic acid is a signaling derivative and is not involved in anaerobic ATP production.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vision is the function of the intermediate retinaldehyde, not retinoic acid.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A physiologist studying mitochondrial ATP synthesis wants to explain the fundamental biological requirement for molecular oxygen. Which statement best accounts for this need?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oxygen directly phosphorylates ADP to form ATP at the inner mitochondrial membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oxygen is a required reagent in every metabolic reaction of the cell, aerobic or not

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oxygen is one of the products released by any combustion reaction of a carbon fuel

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxygen is reduced to water in the terminal step of the electron transport chain

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oxygen is required for the reduction of all vitamin-derived coenzymes such as NAD+ and FAD

explanation.summary: Oxygen is essential as the terminal electron acceptor of the ETC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxygen is predominantly consumed in the electron transport chain, where it serves as the terminal electron acceptor and is reduced to water. Without oxygen, electrons cannot pass along the chain, the proton gradient collapses, and ETC-driven ATP production ceases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP synthase phosphorylates ADP using the proton gradient; oxygen does not directly phosphorylate ADP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glycolysis and other pathways proceed anaerobically, so oxygen is not a reagent in every metabolic reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxygen is a reagent (substrate) of combustion, not a product; the products are water and carbon dioxide.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vitamin-derived cofactors such as NADH can be reduced without oxygen present.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Oxidative catabolism of a single 16-carbon fatty acid generates substantially more ATP than catabolism of a 6-carbon glucose molecule. Which principle best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A larger, more oxidizable carbon substrate produces more reduced coenzymes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fatty acid catabolism does not require oxygen at any step of its pathway

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fatty acids are catabolized completely without ever producing carbon dioxide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fatty acids can be catabolized anaerobically in the cytosol whereas glucose cannot

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glucose catabolism yields no ATP once its six carbons are fully oxidized

explanation.summary: The more a carbon substrate can be oxidized, the more reduced coenzymes and ATP it yields.
explanation.whyCorrect: The more a carbon substrate can be oxidized, the more reduced coenzymes are produced to drive ATP synthesis through the ETC. A fatty acid containing 10-20 carbons can be oxidized far more than a six-carbon glucose molecule, so it yields more ATP.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fatty acid oxidation is an aerobic mitochondrial process that requires oxygen for the ETC.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Carbons of fatty acids are oxidized to carbon dioxide, the most oxidized form of carbon in the body.
whyWrongByChoice.D: It is glucose (via glycolysis) that can be catabolized anaerobically; fatty acid oxidation requires oxygen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glucose catabolism does yield ATP; it simply yields less than a long fatty acid.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Among the major biomolecules, which class is oxidatively catabolized but, unlike the others, does not yield ATP?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amino acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carbohydrate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lipid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nucleotide

explanation.summary: Nucleotide catabolism is the exception that does not generate ATP.
explanation.whyCorrect: While nucleotides are oxidatively catabolized, this process is not linked to ATP production. This is the stated exception to the rule that oxidative catabolism of carbon substrates yields ATP.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amino acids have enzymatic pathways that feed catabolism and produce ATP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbohydrates such as glucose are oxidatively catabolized to produce ATP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycogen is a stored carbohydrate that is broken to glucose and ultimately yields ATP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lipids are catabolized through fatty acid oxidation to produce large amounts of ATP.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with iron-deficiency anemia and a low hematocrit reports fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion. Which mechanism best explains her symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accumulation of NADH from anaerobic glycolysis in all tissues

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess oxygen delivery driving overproduction of ATP

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucagon excess forcing continuous gluconeogenesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insulin deficiency preventing cellular glucose uptake

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced oxygen delivery limiting ATP production in tissues

explanation.summary: Anemia limits oxygen delivery, which limits the product of the combustion-like reaction: ATP.
explanation.whyCorrect: In anemia, decreased red blood cell mass diminishes oxygen delivery capacity. Because oxygen is a required substrate for maximal ATP production, tissue ATP falls, producing fatigue, exhaustion, and dyspnea on exertion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Her limitation is oxygen substrate availability, not a generalized buildup of NADH from anaerobic glycolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anemia decreases, not increases, oxygen delivery, so ATP production is reduced rather than overproduced.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucagon-driven gluconeogenesis is not the mechanism of anemia-related fatigue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Her symptoms stem from impaired oxygen delivery, not from insulin deficiency or defective glucose uptake.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes has a chronic, non-healing foot ulcer, and his physician recommends hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT). What is the primary rationale for this treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: HBOT delivers about 100% oxygen to raise tissue oxygen and restore ATP

choices.label: B
choices.text: HBOT directly lowers blood glucose levels in the poorly perfused limb

choices.label: C
choices.text: HBOT supplies enough oxygen to eliminate the healing tissue's need for the electron transport chain

choices.label: D
choices.text: HBOT reduces the patient's daily insulin requirement by roughly half

choices.label: E
choices.text: HBOT supplies an additional carbon substrate that is oxidized for ATP

explanation.summary: HBOT overcomes poor peripheral oxygen delivery to restore ATP needed for wound healing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hyperglycemia damages vessels through glycation and impairs perfusion, lowering peripheral oxygen delivery and hindering ATP production. Because wound healing is energetically expensive, HBOT provides an enriched environment of about 100% oxygen (versus about 21% in the atmosphere) to restore ATP production and promote wound closure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: HBOT supplies oxygen; it does not directly lower blood glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HBOT supplies the ETC's oxygen substrate; it does not remove the need for the ETC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HBOT does not act on insulin requirements; it corrects an oxygen delivery deficit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor, not a carbon substrate that is oxidized for ATP.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Approximately three hours after a carbohydrate-rich meal, a healthy adult is in the absorptive state. Which hormone predominates, and which pathway is favored to store the excess glucose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glucagon; fatty acid oxidation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucagon; gluconeogenesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucagon; glycogenolysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insulin; glycogenesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Insulin; lipolysis

explanation.summary: In the fed state, insulin drives anabolic storage of glucose as glycogen.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the fed (postprandial, absorptive) state, insulin is abundant and anabolic pathways such as glycogenesis in the liver and skeletal muscle predominate to store carbons for later fasting states.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fatty acid oxidation and glucagon characterize fasting, not the fed absorptive state.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gluconeogenesis is a glucagon-driven catabolic response of prolonged fasting.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucagon and glycogenolysis dominate the fasting state, not the fed state.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Insulin does predominate, but it promotes storage (glycogenesis/lipogenesis), not lipolysis.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A 12-year-old girl presents with unexplained weight loss and is diagnosed with new-onset type 1 diabetes caused by insulin insufficiency. Compared with an unaffected child, which metabolic function is most diminished in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glucagon promoting anabolic processes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucagon promoting catabolic processes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Insulin promoting anabolic processes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insulin promoting catabolic processes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oxygen delivery to peripheral tissues

explanation.summary: Insulin is an anabolic hormone, so its deficiency diminishes anabolic storage and causes weight loss.
explanation.whyCorrect: Insulin is an anabolic hormone that promotes storage of glucose into glycogen and can stimulate lipogenesis. In insulin insufficiency, the loss of anabolic signaling accounts for the unexplained weight loss, so insulin-driven anabolic processes are diminished.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glucagon promotes catabolism, not anabolism, so this pairing is incorrect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Diminished glucagon-driven catabolism would not cause weight loss; increased catabolism, not decreased, promotes weight loss.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Insulin is anabolic, not catabolic, so it does not promote catabolic processes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oxygen delivery is not the primary metabolic deficit in insulin insufficiency.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: At the terminal step of the electron transport chain, molecular oxygen accepts electrons and is converted to water. According to the metabolic definitions of oxidation and reduction, the conversion of O2 to H2O is classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A reduction, because oxygen gains bonds to hydrogen

choices.label: B
choices.text: A reduction, because oxygen gains bonds to nitrogen

choices.label: C
choices.text: An oxidation, because oxygen gains bonds to hydrogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: An oxidation, because oxygen loses bonds to oxygen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neither, because the oxidation state of oxygen is unchanged

explanation.summary: Reduction is the gain of bonds to hydrogen and/or the loss of bonds to oxygen, nitrogen, or sulfur.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxygen serves as the terminal electron acceptor of the ETC and is ultimately reduced to water. Converting O2 to H2O adds bonds to hydrogen, which obeys the gain-of-bonds-to-hydrogen rule for reduction.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Water contains no nitrogen; gaining bonds to nitrogen would be an oxidation in any case.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gaining bonds to hydrogen defines reduction, not oxidation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Loss of bonds to oxygen is a reduction, and oxygen becoming water is a gain of hydrogen bonds, not a loss of oxygen bonds.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oxygen is changed; it accepts electrons and is reduced to water at the end of the chain.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Within a cell, a protein is broken down into peptides and single amino acids. This process is best classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anabolic; energy is consumed in the form of ATP

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anabolic; energy is released as heat

choices.label: C
choices.text: Anabolic; no net energy change occurs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Catabolic; energy is consumed as ATP

choices.label: E
choices.text: Catabolic; energy released as heat or ATP

explanation.summary: Catabolism breaks complex molecules into smaller ones with concomitant energy release as heat or ATP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Catabolic processes involve the breakdown of complex molecules into smaller ones with concomitant energy release in the form of heat or ATP. The breakdown of proteins into peptides or single amino acids is the brick's example of a catabolic process.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anabolism builds smaller molecules into larger ones; breaking a protein apart is the opposite.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Protein breakdown is catabolic, not anabolic, and anabolism consumes rather than releases energy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Protein breakdown is catabolic and is accompanied by energy release, not a neutral energy balance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Catabolism releases energy rather than consuming ATP.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: The synthesis of tyrosine from phenylalanine is catabolic from the perspective of phenylalanine, which is consumed. When the global pathway and its net result are considered instead, the enzymatic cascade is best designated as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anabolic, because a new amino acid is synthesized

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anabolic, because ATP is generated in the process

choices.label: C
choices.text: Catabolic, because energy is released as heat

choices.label: D
choices.text: Catabolic, because phenylalanine is consumed

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neither, because no coenzyme participates

explanation.summary: Pathways should be judged by the transformation of each molecule and also by the global net result.
explanation.whyCorrect: When considering pathways it is best to reference the transformation each molecule undergoes but also consider the global pathway and its net result. Anabolic is the correct designation for this cascade because its end product is the synthesis of a new amino acid, tyrosine.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Anabolic processes are energy dependent and consume ATP; generating ATP is not the reason for the anabolic designation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The net result is synthesis of a new molecule; the pathway is not designated catabolic on the basis of heat release.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Consumption of phenylalanine makes the step catabolic only from phenylalanine's own perspective, not for the overall pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pathway can be classified; the overall designation is anabolic because a new amino acid is produced.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A hydroxylase is found to catalyze an oxidation-reduction reaction. Like dehydrogenases, oxidases, reductases, and peroxidases, this enzyme requires a coenzyme. In these reactions, the coenzyme primarily serves as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A carbon substrate that is oxidized

choices.label: B
choices.text: A source of high-energy phosphate

choices.label: C
choices.text: A terminal electron acceptor

choices.label: D
choices.text: An allosteric inhibitor of the enzyme

choices.label: E
choices.text: An electron shuttle

explanation.summary: Oxidoreductase reactions require a coenzyme that serves as an electron shuttle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxidation and reduction reactions are catalyzed by oxidoreductase enzymes such as dehydrogenases, oxidases, reductases, hydroxylases, and peroxidases. These reactions require a coenzyme that serves as an electron shuttle; vitamin B-derived coenzymes such as NAD+, FAD, and NADP+ are very common in this role.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The carbon substrate is the biomolecule being oxidized; the coenzyme shuttles the electrons removed from it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The coenzyme carries electrons; it is not a phosphate donor like ATP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxygen, not the coenzyme, is the terminal electron acceptor at the end of the ETC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The coenzyme is required for the reaction to proceed; it does not inhibit the enzyme.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of coenzymes is derived from B vitamins and commonly participates in oxidation/reduction reactions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ATP and ADP

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucose and pyruvate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Insulin and glucagon

choices.label: D
choices.text: NAD+ and FAD

choices.label: E
choices.text: Retinol and retinoic acid

explanation.summary: NAD+, FAD, and NADP+ are vitamin B-derived coenzymes that are very common in oxidation/reduction reactions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vitamin B-derived coenzymes such as NAD+, FAD, and NADP+ serve as electron shuttles and are very common in oxidation/reduction reactions catalyzed by oxidoreductase enzymes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP and ADP are energy currency molecules, not vitamin B-derived electron shuttles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glucose and pyruvate are carbon substrates of glycolysis, not coenzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin and glucagon are hormones that govern substrate availability, not coenzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Retinol and retinoic acid are vitamin A and its oxidized derivative, substrates of oxidation rather than B vitamin-derived coenzymes.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A tissue lacking molecular oxygen (anaerobic conditions) continues to catabolize glucose to pyruvate by glycolysis. Which of the following correctly describes the redox status of glucose in this pathway?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glucose is neither oxidized nor reduced without oxygen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucose is oxidized even though molecular oxygen is absent

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucose is oxidized only after oxygen is restored

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glucose is reduced because molecular oxygen is not available

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glucose is reduced while NAD+ is oxidized to NADH

explanation.summary: The term oxidation is not restricted to reactions that require oxygen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxygen may or may not be explicitly involved in an oxidative cascade, and the terminology can be misleading. Glycolysis can occur under anaerobic conditions but still oxidizes glucose, producing NADH from NAD+ in the process.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glucose is oxidatively catabolized to pyruvate whether or not oxygen is present.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycolysis oxidizes glucose under anaerobic conditions; it does not wait for oxygen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Absence of oxygen does not reverse the chemistry; glucose is still oxidized in glycolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glucose is the molecule oxidized, and NAD+ is reduced (not oxidized) to NADH.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) catalyzes the second oxidative step in the biotransformation of vitamin A. Which of the following functional group changes occurs in this step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alcohol (CH2OH) to aldehyde (CHO)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alcohol (CH2OH) to carboxylic acid (COOH)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aldehyde (CHO) to alcohol (CH2OH)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aldehyde (CHO) to carboxylic acid (COOH)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Carboxylic acid (COOH) to aldehyde (CHO)

explanation.summary: ALDH oxidizes the aldehyde of retinaldehyde to the carboxylic acid of retinoic acid.
explanation.whyCorrect: In Figure 1, retinol carries a CH2OH group, retinaldehyde a CHO group, and retinoic acid a COOH group. Aldehyde dehydrogenase converts retinaldehyde (CHO) to retinoic acid (COOH) while NAD+ is reduced to NADH, illustrating how oxidation alters functional groups to create bioactive derivatives.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alcohol to aldehyde is the first step, catalyzed by alcohol dehydrogenase, not ALDH.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Alcohol to carboxylic acid spans both steps; ALDH alone only converts the aldehyde to the acid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aldehyde to alcohol is a reduction and is not the ALDH step.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Carboxylic acid to aldehyde would be a reduction, the reverse of what ALDH does.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A researcher isolates the vitamin A derivative that bears an aldehyde (CHO) functional group. This derivative is most important for which function, and which enzyme produces it from retinol?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Embryonic development; aldehyde dehydrogenase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immunity; alcohol dehydrogenase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tissue maintenance; alcohol dehydrogenase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vision; alcohol dehydrogenase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vision; aldehyde dehydrogenase

explanation.summary: Retinaldehyde, the aldehyde intermediate made by alcohol dehydrogenase, functions in vision.
explanation.whyCorrect: Alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) oxidizes largely inert retinol (CH2OH) to retinaldehyde (CHO). Retinaldehyde is the vitamin A derivative responsible for vision, whereas further oxidation by aldehyde dehydrogenase yields retinoic acid.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Embryonic development is a function of retinoic acid, produced by aldehyde dehydrogenase from the aldehyde.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immunity is a function of retinoic acid, the carboxylic acid product, not of the aldehyde.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tissue maintenance is a role of retinoic acid, not retinaldehyde.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vision is correct, but aldehyde dehydrogenase acts on retinaldehyde, not on retinol; ADH makes the aldehyde.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: During fatty acid synthesis, the growing carbon chain undergoes multiple reduction steps that require NADPH. Which of the following correctly describes the coenzyme change and the overall classification of the pathway?

choices.label: A
choices.text: NADP+ is oxidized to NADPH; the pathway is oxidative

choices.label: B
choices.text: NADP+ is reduced to NADPH; the pathway is reductive

choices.label: C
choices.text: NADPH is oxidized to NADP+; the pathway is oxidative

choices.label: D
choices.text: NADPH is oxidized to NADP+; the pathway is reductive

choices.label: E
choices.text: NADPH is reduced to NADP+; the pathway is reductive

explanation.summary: A pathway's oxidative or reductive label refers to the biomolecule, not the vitamin-derived cofactor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fatty acid synthesis is considered reductive based on the multiple steps in which the carbon chain is reduced. To be reduced, the reductive power of NADPH is required, and as carbons are extended NADPH is converted to NADP+, which is an oxidation of the cofactor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: NADP+ to NADPH would be a reduction of the cofactor and is not what occurs here, and the pathway is reductive.
whyWrongByChoice.B: In fatty acid synthesis NADPH is consumed to NADP+, not generated from NADP+.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The coenzyme change is right, but the pathway is classified by the biomolecule, which is reduced, so it is reductive.
whyWrongByChoice.E: NADPH to NADP+ is an oxidation of the coenzyme, not a reduction.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A biochemist studies a tissue in which an overall anabolic pathway is actively synthesizing a macromolecule. Which of the following is most likely produced as a direct consequence of the coenzyme chemistry of this pathway?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ca++

choices.label: B
choices.text: FADH2

choices.label: C
choices.text: NADH

choices.label: D
choices.text: NADP+

choices.label: E
choices.text: O2

explanation.summary: Anabolic pathways reduce carbons and therefore oxidize their coenzymes, yielding oxidized coenzyme forms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Anabolic pathways typically reduce carbons to build macromolecules. In the process, coenzymes must be oxidized, so anabolic pathways generally yield oxidized forms of coenzymes such as NADP+ (for example, NADPH converted to NADP+ during fatty acid synthesis).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ca++ is a micronutrient required for metabolism, but its oxidation state is not altered.
whyWrongByChoice.B: FADH2 is a reduced coenzyme produced during catabolic pathways, not anabolic ones.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NADH is a reduced coenzyme produced during oxidative catabolic pathways such as glycolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: O2 is not produced by metabolism; it is consumed in the electron transport chain.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: The metabolic requirement for molecular oxygen is illustrated by a generic combustion reaction in which a carbon source reacts with O2. Which of the following are the products of this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carbon dioxide, hydrogen, and heat

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucose, ATP, and heat

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycogen, carbon dioxide, and water

choices.label: D
choices.text: Water, carbon dioxide, and energy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Water, oxygen, and energy

explanation.summary: Carbon source + O2 yields H2O + CO2 + energy.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the generic combustion reaction, carbons are oxidized to carbon dioxide, oxygen is reduced to water, and energy is released as ATP or heat. Biomacromolecules such as carbohydrates are carbon sources that can combust if oxygen is present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hydrogen gas is not a product; hydrogen ends up in water formed by reduction of oxygen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glucose is a carbon source (a reactant), not a product of combustion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycogen is a storage form of glucose built during the fed state, not a combustion product.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oxygen is a reagent of combustion, not one of its products.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: In the combustion of a carbon source with molecular oxygen in the human body, which product is formed by the reduction of O2, and which product represents the most oxidized form of carbon?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ATP; carbon dioxide

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carbon dioxide; water

choices.label: C
choices.text: Heat; water

choices.label: D
choices.text: Water; ATP

choices.label: E
choices.text: Water; carbon dioxide

explanation.summary: Water comes from reduction of O2, and carbon dioxide is the most oxidized form of carbon in the body.
explanation.whyCorrect: During combustion, carbons are oxidized to yield carbon dioxide, the most oxidized form of carbon in the human body, while water is produced from the reduction of O2. The remaining product is energy in the form of ATP or heat.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP is the energy product; it is not formed by reduction of O2.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The pairing is reversed: carbon dioxide comes from oxidized carbon, and water comes from reduced oxygen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Heat is energy, not a reduction product of oxygen, and water is not a form of carbon.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Water is correct for the first part, but ATP is not a form of carbon.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Electrons from reduced coenzymes pass through the protein complexes of the ETC much like electrons flowing through a wire. The energy of this electron flow is directly used to accomplish which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oxidize water to regenerate molecular oxygen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Phosphorylate ADP at each protein complex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pump protons from the intermembrane space into the matrix

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduce NAD+ to NADH within the matrix

choices.label: E
choices.text: Translocate protons into the intermembrane space

explanation.summary: Electron flow through the ETC powers proton translocation into the intermembrane space, creating a charge gradient.
explanation.whyCorrect: The passing of electrons from reduced coenzymes through the ETC complexes is a form of energy used to translocate protons into the intermembrane space of the mitochondria, generating a gradient of charge that is later used to produce ATP.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oxygen is reduced to water at the end of the chain; water is not oxidized back to oxygen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ADP is phosphorylated by ATP synthase using the proton gradient, not at each complex by electron flow.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Protons are pumped out of the matrix into the intermembrane space; their return to the matrix occurs through ATP synthase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: NADH is produced when carbon substrates are oxidized during catabolism; the ETC consumes the reduction potential of NADH.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: The charge gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane is utilized to synthesize ATP. Which of the following events directly drives ATP production?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Electrons passing from oxygen back to the ETC complexes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oxygen entering the matrix to bind ATP synthase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protons being pumped out of the matrix by ATP synthase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Protons diffusing freely across the outer membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Protons returning to the matrix through ATP synthase

explanation.summary: ATP is produced when protons selectively pass back into the matrix through ATP synthase.
explanation.whyCorrect: The charge gradient generated by proton translocation is utilized to produce ATP when the protons selectively pass through the inner membrane via ATP synthase to return to the matrix.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Electrons flow from reduced coenzymes through the complexes onto oxygen; oxygen does not return electrons to the chain.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Oxygen's role is to accept electrons and be reduced to water; it does not bind ATP synthase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Protons are pumped out of the matrix by the ETC complexes; ATP synthase is the route by which they return.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ATP synthesis depends on protons passing selectively through ATP synthase in the inner membrane, not free diffusion across the outer membrane.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A hyperbaric oxygen therapy unit lists the conditions it treats. Which of the following listed indications is noted as not fully proven in a medical context?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bites from venomous snakes or spiders

choices.label: B
choices.text: Burns with delayed wound healing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decompression sickness after diving

choices.label: D
choices.text: Flesh-eating necrotizing infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recovery from extreme exertion

explanation.summary: Among HBOT indications, recovery from extreme exertion is flagged as not fully proven medically.
explanation.whyCorrect: The spectrum of conditions that may require HBOT includes burns, flesh-eating disease, bites from venomous species, decompression sickness, and recovery from extreme exertion; the last of these is specifically noted as not fully proven in a medical context.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bites from venomous species are listed as an HBOT indication without the unproven caveat.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Burns are listed as an established condition that may require HBOT.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Decompression sickness is a listed HBOT indication without the unproven caveat.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Flesh-eating disease is listed as a condition that may require HBOT without the unproven caveat.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman with long-standing hyperglycemia has a foot ulcer that has failed to heal for several months. Which of the following best explains the impaired healing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated glucagon diverts carbon substrates away from the wound

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess glucose directly inhibits ATP synthase in wound tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycation damages vessels, reducing perfusion and oxygen delivery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hyperglycemia depletes NAD+ so that oxidation cannot proceed

choices.label: E
choices.text: Insulin excess suppresses catabolism needed for tissue repair

explanation.summary: Hyperglycemia damages vessels through glycation, impairing perfusion and peripheral oxygen delivery.
explanation.whyCorrect: Foot ulcers do not properly heal in a diabetic patient because hyperglycemia damages vessels through glycation, adversely impacting blood perfusion and therefore peripheral oxygen delivery. Lower oxygen delivery hinders ATP production, and because wound healing is energetically expensive, the lack of oxygen impedes proper healing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glucagon governs fasting metabolism; it is not the mechanism of impaired diabetic wound healing.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The defect is upstream at the level of oxygen delivery through damaged vessels, not direct inhibition of ATP synthase by glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The limiting factor is oxygen substrate availability from poor perfusion, not depletion of NAD+.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Diabetic ulcers arise from hyperglycemia-related vessel damage, not from excess insulin.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Metabolism is a series of enzymatically catalyzed reactions. HBOT raises the relative oxygen abundance on the outside of a poorly perfused tissue in order to increase ATP formation. This strategy relies on which general principle?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accumulated product accelerates the forward reaction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enzyme quantity, rather than substrate, limits product formation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased pressure converts anabolic pathways to catabolic

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxygen acts as a coenzyme regenerated after each reaction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Substrate availability determines the extent of product formation

explanation.summary: In enzymatically catalyzed metabolism, the relative abundance of substrates determines the extent of product formation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because metabolism is a series of enzymatically catalyzed chemical reactions, the relative abundance of substrates determines the extent of product formation. When oxygen delivery is compromised, HBOT supplies additional oxygen substrate so that ATP production can be restored and wound closure promoted.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Raising oxygen increases a reactant, not a product; product accumulation is not the driver.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HBOT works by increasing substrate (oxygen) supply, which shows that substrate availability, not enzyme quantity, is what limits ATP formation here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HBOT does not convert anabolic pathways to catabolic ones; it restores oxygen substrate for ATP production.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxygen is a substrate that is consumed and reduced to water, not a regenerated coenzyme.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A healthy 30-year-old man eats dinner at 7 PM and has his next meal at 8 AM. At 6 AM, which hormone predominates and which pathway is prevalent to maintain his blood glucose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glucagon; glycogenesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucagon; glycogenolysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Insulin; glycogenesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insulin; glycogenolysis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Insulin; lipogenesis

explanation.summary: In the fasting (postabsorptive) state, glucagon predominates and glycogenolysis maintains blood glucose.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the fasting (postabsorptive) state, food intake has been restricted for more than 4 hours, such as overnight. Insulin tapers off while glucagon becomes prevalent, and catabolic pathways such as glycogenolysis predominate in an effort to maintain blood glucose levels.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glucagon is correct, but it stimulates glycogen mobilization (glycogenolysis), not glycogen synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin and glycogenesis characterize the fed state within about 3-4 hours of eating, not an overnight fast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glycogenolysis is correct, but it is driven by glucagon after insulin has tapered off.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Insulin-driven conversion of glucose to lipids occurs when glucose is sustained and abundant, not during fasting.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A 27-year-old hiker is rescued after 3 days without any food. Which of the following best describes his hepatic glycogen stores and the processes maintaining his blood glucose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glycogen depleted; gluconeogenesis and amino acid catabolism

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glycogen depleted; insulin-driven lipogenesis supplies glucose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycogen partially depleted; dietary glucose is the main substrate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glycogen replete; glycogenesis stores incoming glucose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glycogen replete; glycogenolysis alone maintains glucose

explanation.summary: In prolonged fasting (2-4 days), hepatic glycogen is depleted and gluconeogenesis, amino acid catabolism, and fatty acid oxidation maintain glucose.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the prolonged fasting (starvation) state, food intake has ceased for 2-4 days, glucagon is high and insulin low, and hepatic glycogen stores are depleted. Processes such as fatty acid oxidation, amino acid catabolism, and gluconeogenesis maintain blood glucose levels, with glucagon promoting lipolysis and protein catabolism to produce glucose via gluconeogenesis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Glycogen depletion is correct, but insulin is low and lipogenesis is an anabolic storage process, not a glucose source.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No dietary glucose is available after 3 days, and hepatic glycogen is fully depleted rather than partially.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glycogenesis requires incoming dietary glucose and insulin, both absent after 3 days of starvation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: After 2-4 days without food, hepatic glycogen is depleted, so glycogenolysis cannot be the sole source of glucose.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: Two hours after a mixed meal, a healthy adult's tissues are actively generating ATP. Which of the following is the predominant substrate for oxidative catabolism at this time?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amino acids from protein catabolism

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dietary glucose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fatty acids mobilized by lipolysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glucose produced by gluconeogenesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hepatic glycogen

explanation.summary: In the fed state, dietary glucose is the predominant substrate for oxidative catabolism.
explanation.whyCorrect: The fed (postprandial or absorptive) state spans roughly 3-4 hours after eating. During this time insulin is abundant and the body utilizes dietary glucose as the predominant substrate for oxidative catabolism, while excess carbons are stored by glycogenesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amino acid catabolism to maintain glucose is a feature of prolonged fasting, not the absorptive state.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipolysis is promoted by glucagon during prolonged glucose deprivation, not 2 hours after a meal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gluconeogenesis is a prolonged-fasting process; dietary glucose is available in the fed state.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hepatic glycogen is being built (glycogenesis) in the fed state, not mobilized as the main fuel.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man consistently eats far more carbohydrate than he needs, so that his glucose levels remain sustained and abundant. Under the influence of insulin, what is the fate of this excess glucose once glycogen depots are filled?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conversion to glucose via gluconeogenesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion to lipids

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excretion as carbon dioxide without ATP production

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mobilization by glycogenolysis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Storage as protein in skeletal muscle

explanation.summary: When glucose is sustained and sufficiently abundant, insulin promotes its conversion to lipids.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the fed state, insulin promotes storage of excess glucose into depots such as glycogen. If glucose levels are sustained and sufficiently abundant, glucose will be converted to lipids.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gluconeogenesis produces glucose during prolonged fasting; it does not dispose of excess glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucose that is oxidized to carbon dioxide yields ATP; excess glucose under insulin is stored, not wasted.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glycogenolysis is a glucagon-driven catabolic process of fasting, not a fate of excess fed-state glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Excess glucose is stored as glycogen and then lipids; it is not stored as protein.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: During the fed state, insulin promotes storage of carbons for use in later fasting states. Glycogenesis predominantly occurs in which of the following tissue pairs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adipose tissue and brain

choices.label: B
choices.text: Brain and skeletal muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kidney and red blood cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Liver and skeletal muscle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pancreas and adipose tissue

explanation.summary: Fed-state glycogenesis predominates in the liver and skeletal muscle.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the fed state insulin is abundant, and anabolic pathways such as glycogenesis in the liver and skeletal muscle predominate to store carbons for future use in fasting states.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adipose tissue and brain are not the sites of glycogenesis described; glycogen storage is in liver and skeletal muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Skeletal muscle is correct, but the brain is not a site of fed-state glycogenesis; the liver is.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Kidney and red blood cells are not the glycogen depots described for the fed state.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pancreas secretes insulin and glucagon; it is not a glycogen storage depot, and adipose is not the site named.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A student argues that glycolysis cannot be an oxidative pathway because it generates NADH, a reduced molecule. Which of the following is the best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glycolysis is neither oxidative nor reductive because it is anabolic

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glycolysis is oxidative only when molecular oxygen is present

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycolysis is reductive because NADH accumulates during the pathway

choices.label: D
choices.text: NADH is an oxidized coenzyme, so glycolysis remains oxidative

choices.label: E
choices.text: The designation refers to glucose, the biomolecule, not the cofactor

explanation.summary: The oxidative/reductive classification of a pathway refers to the biomolecule itself, not the vitamin-derived cofactor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Catabolic pathways are generally oxidative and anabolic pathways reductive, but this generalization refers to the biomolecule itself and not the required vitamin-derived cofactors. In glycolysis, glucose is oxidatively catabolized to pyruvate, and in the process NADH is produced from NAD+; the pathway is still classified as oxidative.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glycolysis is catabolic (it breaks glucose down to pyruvate), and it is classified as oxidative.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glycolysis oxidizes glucose even under anaerobic conditions; oxygen is not required for the oxidative designation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NADH production reflects reduction of the cofactor; the biomolecule glucose is oxidized, so the pathway is oxidative.
whyWrongByChoice.D: NADH is the reduced form of the coenzyme; the argument that it is oxidized is factually wrong.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: In the biotransformation of vitamin A, retinol is converted to retinaldehyde by alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH), and retinaldehyde is converted to retinoic acid by aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH). Which statement best describes these two steps with respect to reversibility and coenzyme use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both steps are irreversible and both reduce NAD+ to NADH

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both steps are reversible and both consume NADH

choices.label: C
choices.text: The ADH step is irreversible; the ALDH step is reversible

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ADH step is reversible; the ALDH step is irreversible

choices.label: E
choices.text: The ADH step uses FAD; the ALDH step uses NAD+

explanation.summary: Retinol and retinaldehyde interconvert via ADH, whereas ALDH oxidation to retinoic acid proceeds in one direction.
explanation.whyCorrect: In Figure 1, the ADH-catalyzed conversion between retinol and retinaldehyde is shown with paired arrows in both directions, with NAD+ reduced to NADH in the forward direction and NADH oxidized to NAD+ in the reverse. The ALDH-catalyzed conversion of retinaldehyde to retinoic acid is shown as a single one-way arrow, with NAD+ reduced to NADH.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The coenzyme change is correct for the forward oxidations, but the ADH step is depicted as reversible, not irreversible.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Only the ADH step is shown as reversible, and the forward oxidations reduce NAD+ to NADH rather than consuming NADH.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The reversibility is backwards: the ADH step is reversible and the ALDH step is one-way.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Both steps use the NAD+/NADH couple; FAD is not the coenzyme in this figure.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions

questions.stem: A researcher maintains a cultured cell line under strictly anaerobic conditions. Despite the complete absence of oxygen, the cells continue to generate ATP. Which of the following processes is most likely responsible for this ATP production?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ATP synthase driven by a proton gradient

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complex IV proton pumping

choices.label: C
choices.text: Electron transport chain activity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxidative phosphorylation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Substrate level phosphorylation

explanation.summary: Substrate level phosphorylation generates ATP without oxygen by directly transferring a phosphoryl group onto ADP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Substrate level phosphorylation produces ATP by direct transfer of a phosphoryl group from a donor compound onto ADP, usually via a kinase, and does not require oxygen. It occurs in select steps of glycolysis in the cytoplasm and in one TCA step, allowing ATP generation even under anaerobic conditions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP synthase depends on the proton gradient established by the oxygen-dependent ETC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complex IV activity is part of the ETC and requires oxygen to proceed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The electron transport chain requires oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor and halts without it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxidative phosphorylation is completely reliant on the presence of oxygen and cannot function anaerobically.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man in septic shock has markedly reduced tissue perfusion, and his serum lactate is elevated. His cells are relying on glycolysis for ATP because oxidative phosphorylation is impaired. Which of the following best explains why lactate is accumulating in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glycolytic flux has decreased below baseline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hepatic gluconeogenesis is consuming the accumulated lactate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lactate dehydrogenase regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can continue

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pyruvate dehydrogenase is converting excess pyruvate to acetyl-CoA

choices.label: E
choices.text: The electron transport chain is reoxidizing NADH more efficiently

explanation.summary: When the ETC cannot reoxidize NADH, LDH converts pyruvate to lactate to regenerate NAD+ and sustain glycolysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: With limited oxygen, ATP production from OXPHOS diminishes and NADH can no longer pass electrons to the ETC. Because glycolysis depends on NAD+, the cell must regenerate NAD+ from NADH apart from the ETC. Lactate dehydrogenase reduces pyruvate to lactate while oxidizing NADH to NAD+, allowing glycolytic substrate level phosphorylation to continue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glycolytic flux increases to compensate for absent OXPHOS; it does not fall.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Impaired perfusion and a low NAD+/NADH state favor lactate production, not its consumption by gluconeogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Under hypoxia pyruvate is diverted to lactate, not efficiently converted to acetyl-CoA for the TCA cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The oxygen-deprived ETC cannot reoxidize NADH, which is precisely why lactate forms.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A physiology student is asked why mature red blood cells depend entirely on lactate production for their energy supply. Which of the following features of the mature erythrocyte best accounts for this dependence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They contain abundant mitochondria optimized for OXPHOS

choices.label: B
choices.text: They generate ATP through gluconeogenesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: They lack mitochondria

choices.label: D
choices.text: They preferentially use fatty acid beta-oxidation

choices.label: E
choices.text: They rely on the electron transport chain for most ATP

explanation.summary: Mature erythrocytes lack mitochondria, so their only route to ATP is glycolysis coupled to lactate production.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mature red blood cells normally lack all membrane-bound organelles, including mitochondria. Without mitochondria, their sole option for energy is substrate level phosphorylation during glycolysis, and ATP production relies on lactate formation. These cells are correspondingly enriched with lactate dehydrogenase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mature erythrocytes lack mitochondria entirely, so they cannot perform OXPHOS.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gluconeogenesis is an energy-consuming pathway and is not how erythrocytes generate ATP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Beta-oxidation occurs in mitochondria, which mature red blood cells do not possess.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The electron transport chain resides in mitochondria, which these cells lack.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 49-year-old man with a long history of heavy alcohol use is found confused and is admitted to the emergency department. Laboratory studies reveal a serum glucose of 50 mg/dL. Ethanol oxidation in his liver has raised the NADH:NAD+ ratio. An elevated ratio of which pathway substrate is most directly responsible for his hypoglycemia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acetate:acetyl-CoA

choices.label: B
choices.text: ADH:ALDH

choices.label: C
choices.text: NADH:NAD+

choices.label: D
choices.text: NADPH:NADP

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pyruvate:lactate

explanation.summary: Ethanol oxidation via ADH and ALDH raises NADH, and the resulting low NAD+/NADH ratio inhibits gluconeogenesis, causing fasting hypoglycemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxidation of ethanol through ADH and ALDH produces an accumulation of NADH in the cytosol and mitochondria. This low NAD+/NADH ratio inhibits gluconeogenesis, so de novo glucose synthesis fails. In individuals who drink routinely and eat poorly, this produces fasting hypoglycemia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This ratio is not the mechanism linking ethanol metabolism to impaired glucose production.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Although alcohol can induce oxidative enzymes, a change in this ratio does not explain the hypoglycemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ethanol metabolism does not significantly alter the NADPH/NADP ratio; this coenzyme is not the driver of hypoglycemia here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Alcohol increases NADH and shifts equilibrium toward lactate, so the pyruvate:lactate ratio is low, not elevated.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man presents with blurred vision progressing toward blindness, headache, and severe nausea after consuming improperly distilled homemade liquor. Laboratory studies show a high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Which metabolite is most directly responsible for his toxicity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acetaldehyde

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acetate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Formic acid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glycolaldehyde

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oxalic acid

explanation.summary: Methanol is converted by ADH to formaldehyde and by ALDH to formic acid, which inhibits the ETC at complex IV and damages the optic nerve.
explanation.whyCorrect: Methanol is metabolized by ADH into formaldehyde and then by ALDH into formic acid. Formic acid blunts ATP formation in the mitochondria by inhibiting the electron transport chain at complex IV. Because the optic nerve and eye are high energy demand tissues, they are especially vulnerable, producing the characteristic visual disturbance and blindness.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetaldehyde is the toxic first metabolite of ethanol and accounts for hangover symptoms, not methanol-induced blindness.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acetate is the non-toxic final product of ethanol oxidation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glycolaldehyde is an intermediate of ethylene glycol metabolism, not methanol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oxalic acid is the toxic end product of ethylene glycol and causes renal failure, not visual loss.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after intentionally ingesting antifreeze. He develops flank pain and acute renal failure, and urinalysis reveals numerous envelope-shaped crystals. Which metabolite of the ingested compound is most directly responsible for his renal injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acetaldehyde

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acetate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Formaldehyde

choices.label: D
choices.text: Formic acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oxalic acid

explanation.summary: Ethylene glycol is oxidized to oxalic acid, which forms calcium oxalate crystals that precipitate in the proximal renal tubule and cause renal failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ethylene glycol, the active chemical in antifreeze, is metabolized by ADH to glycolaldehyde and by ALDH to glyoxylic acid, which is converted to oxalic acid. Oxalic acid forms calcium oxalate crystals that precipitate in the proximal renal tubule, producing the hallmark folded-envelope shaped crystals and renal failure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetaldehyde is the intermediate of ethanol metabolism and is responsible for hangover symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acetate is the harmless final product of ethanol oxidation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Formaldehyde is the intermediate metabolite of methanol, not ethylene glycol.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Formic acid is the toxic metabolite of methanol and causes blindness by inhibiting the ETC, not envelope-shaped renal crystals.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 3-year-old refugee child is brought to a clinic with abdominal distension, a palpable enlarged liver, and peripheral pitting edema. His caloric intake had been adequate but consisted almost entirely of protein-poor grain products. Which mechanism best explains the child's edema?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased hepatic albumin production lowering plasma oncotic pressure

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deposition of calcium oxalate crystals in the renal tubules

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated blood glucose causing osmotic fluid shifts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excessive oxidative catabolism of muscle and subcutaneous fat

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased plasma oncotic pressure drawing fluid into vessels

explanation.summary: Kwashiorkor results from protein deficiency; decreased hepatic albumin lowers oncotic pressure, driving fluid from the intravascular into the extravascular space.
explanation.whyCorrect: This child has kwashiorkor, a severe protein deficiency with adequate overall calories. Decreased protein intake decreases hepatic albumin production, which decreases oncotic pressure. The fall in oncotic pressure causes water to move from the intravascular into the extravascular space, producing edema, while decreased lipoprotein production causes the associated hepatomegaly.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Calcium oxalate deposition is a feature of ethylene glycol poisoning, unrelated to protein malnutrition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Kwashiorkor edema is driven by low albumin, not by hyperglycemia-related osmotic shifts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxidative catabolism of muscle and fat characterizes marasmus, which presents with wasting rather than edema.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oncotic pressure is decreased, not increased; a rise would retain fluid in vessels and prevent edema.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 2-year-old child in a drought-stricken region has had almost no access to food of any kind for weeks. On examination he weighs far too little for his height, has broomstick extremities with loss of subcutaneous fat, and no edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic malnutrition with stunting

choices.label: B
choices.text: Kwashiorkor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Marasmic kwashiorkor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Marasmus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Refeeding syndrome

explanation.summary: Marasmus is a generalized caloric deficiency producing wasting, broomstick extremities, and loss of subcutaneous fat without edema.
explanation.whyCorrect: Marasmus is the most common form of acute malnutrition and reflects insufficient calories across all dietary components (fat, carbohydrate, and protein). Muscle and fat are oxidatively catabolized for energy, producing broomstick extremities and loss of subcutaneous fat so the child appears as only skin and bones. The absence of edema distinguishes it from kwashiorkor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic malnutrition presents with stunting and decreased head circumference rather than acute wasting from sudden food loss.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Kwashiorkor is a specific protein deficiency with adequate calories and is characterized by edema, which this child lacks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Marasmic kwashiorkor combines features of both states, including edema, and is the least common form.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Refeeding syndrome is a complication of reintroducing nutrients, not a presenting malnutrition state.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with an altered mental status and a suspected toxic ingestion. Her basic metabolic panel shows Na+ 140 mEq/L, K+ 4.2 mEq/L, Cl- 104 mEq/L, and HCO3- 8 mEq/L. Using the standard formula that excludes potassium, what is her calculated anion gap?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 8 mEq/L

choices.label: B
choices.text: 12 mEq/L

choices.label: C
choices.text: 20 mEq/L

choices.label: D
choices.text: 28 mEq/L

choices.label: E
choices.text: 32 mEq/L

explanation.summary: Anion gap equals Na+ minus (Cl- plus HCO3-); here 140 - (104 + 8) = 28 mEq/L, a high anion gap.
explanation.whyCorrect: The anion gap is calculated as AG = Na+ - (Cl- + HCO3-). Substituting the values gives 140 - (104 + 8) = 28 mEq/L. Because normal ranges are roughly 8-16 mEq/L, this elevated value signifies a high anion gap metabolic acidosis consistent with toxic alcohol ingestion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 8 mEq/L would only result from subtracting incorrectly; it does not match the given values.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 12 mEq/L would fall within the normal range and does not reflect this patient's low bicarbonate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 20 mEq/L is arithmetically incorrect for these values.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 32 mEq/L overestimates the gap; the correct subtraction yields 28.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 6-month-old infant presents with hepatomegaly, a doll-like face, profound fasting hypoglycemia, and lactic acidosis. Studies confirm that glucose 6-phosphate produced from glycogenolysis cannot be converted to free glucose for release into the blood. Deficiency of which enzyme best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alcohol dehydrogenase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aldehyde dehydrogenase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucose 6-phosphatase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lactate dehydrogenase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pyruvate dehydrogenase

explanation.summary: Von Gierke's disease is a glucose 6-phosphatase deficiency causing fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis from excess pyruvate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Von Gierke's disease (Type I glycogen storage disease) is a deficiency of glucose 6-phosphatase in the liver. Glucose 6-phosphate from glycogenolysis cannot be transformed into free glucose for systemic release, causing fasting hypoglycemia. The buildup of glucose 6-phosphate yields excess pyruvate, which is shunted into lactate and produces lactic acidosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alcohol dehydrogenase acts on ethanol and other alcohols, not on glucose metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aldehyde dehydrogenase oxidizes aldehydes in alcohol metabolism and is unrelated to glycogen storage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lactate dehydrogenase deficiency would impair lactate formation, not cause its accumulation with hypoglycemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency causes lactic acidosis but does not block conversion of glucose 6-phosphate to glucose.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A neonate presents with lethargy and a persistent lactic acidosis. Laboratory studies show elevated levels of both pyruvate and lactate. The defect prevents pyruvate, the final product of glycolysis, from entering the TCA cycle. Which of the following best explains this child's lactic acidosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of mitochondria forces reliance on glycolysis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Formic acid inhibits the electron transport chain at complex IV

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucose 6-phosphatase deficiency blocks glucose release from the liver

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased NADH from ethanol oxidation drives pyruvate to lactate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pyruvate cannot be converted to acetyl-CoA and is shunted to lactate

explanation.summary: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency prevents conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA, so accumulating pyruvate is driven into lactate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency prevents the conversion of pyruvate, the final product of glycolysis, into acetyl-CoA, the first reactant of the TCA cycle. The lack of acetyl-CoA production causes an energy decrement, and because pyruvate accumulates through underutilization, equilibrium shifts to produce lactate, yielding lactic acidosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The vignette describes an enzyme block, not an absence of mitochondria; erythrocytes exemplify the latter.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Formic acid inhibition of the ETC is a feature of methanol poisoning, not an enzyme deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucose 6-phosphatase deficiency defines von Gierke's disease and acts upstream on glucose 6-phosphate, not on pyruvate entry into the TCA cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no ethanol exposure in a neonate; the lactic acidosis stems from a pyruvate metabolism defect.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man with a long history of routine heavy alcohol consumption develops severe hepatotoxicity after taking a standard dose of acetaminophen. Induction of which enzyme by his chronic alcohol use best accounts for his increased susceptibility to acetaminophen poisoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alcohol dehydrogenase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aldehyde dehydrogenase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Catalase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cytochrome P450 2E1

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lactate dehydrogenase

explanation.summary: CYP2E1 is enriched in hepatic microsomes and induced by routine excess alcohol, making it clinically relevant in acetaminophen poisoning.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cytochrome P450 2E1 isoform (CYP2E1) is enriched in hepatic microsomes and is induced when alcohol consumption is excessive and routine. This alcohol-dependent induction becomes medically relevant in acetaminophen poisoning and select forms of porphyria, because increased CYP2E1 activity increases conversion of substrates into harmful metabolites.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alcohol dehydrogenase is the major first-step enzyme of ethanol oxidation but is not the inducible microsomal enzyme tied to acetaminophen toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aldehyde dehydrogenase catalyzes the final oxidative step and is not the enzyme induced to worsen acetaminophen toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Catalase resides in peroxisomes and metabolizes only a very small amount of alcohol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lactate dehydrogenase interconverts pyruvate and lactate and has no role in acetaminophen metabolism.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A first-year medical student learns that adult humans would need to consume approximately 65 kg (~140 lbs) of ATP daily to meet their energetic needs, an amount that is untenable. Instead, metabolic ATP generation relies on cyclically regenerating ATP from ADP. Approximately how many times does a single molecule of ADP/ATP cycle each day?

explanation.summary: A single ADP/ATP molecule cycles approximately 1,500 times daily, which is how the body meets a demand equivalent to ~65 kg of ATP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because consuming 65 kg of ATP daily is impossible, ATP generation contains a mechanism to cyclically regenerate ATP from ADP. Each ADP/ATP molecule cycles approximately 1,500 times per day, which highlights the critical nature of the two ATP-generating processes, substrate level phosphorylation and oxidative phosphorylation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cycling only 15 times daily would fall far short of the body's ATP demand.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 150 cycles daily is an order of magnitude below the stated turnover.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 15,000 cycles daily overstates the turnover by a factor of ten.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 150,000 cycles daily is one hundred times the stated figure.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: In a biochemistry laboratory exercise, a student examines the structural change that occurs when pyruvate is converted to lactate by lactate dehydrogenase (LDH). Which of the following best describes the chemical change at the second carbon of pyruvate during this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A phosphoryl group is transferred onto the carbonyl carbon

choices.label: B
choices.text: The carbonyl is oxidized to a second carboxylic acid

choices.label: C
choices.text: The carboxylate group is removed as carbon dioxide

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ketone carbonyl is reduced to a hydroxyl group

choices.label: E
choices.text: The methyl group is oxidized to an aldehyde

explanation.summary: Lactate formation is a reduction of pyruvate in which the ketone carbonyl becomes a hydroxyl group while NADH is oxidized to NAD+.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lactate is produced from the reduction of pyruvate while NADH is oxidized to NAD+. The site of reduction is the carbonyl (C=O) at the second carbon of pyruvate, which becomes a hydroxyl (OH) group in lactate. The reaction is fully reversible and driven by equilibrium, and its purpose is to regenerate NAD+ so glycolysis can sustain substrate level phosphorylation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: LDH is a dehydrogenase; no phosphoryl transfer occurs in this reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The reaction is a reduction, not an oxidation, of the carbonyl carbon.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No carbon is lost; the carboxylate of pyruvate is retained in lactate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The methyl group is unchanged; only the carbonyl carbon is modified.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman has a routine laboratory panel that shows an elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) level. Her physician suspects hemolysis but notes that LDH is expressed in a variety of tissues. Which of the following additional findings would most strongly support a diagnosis of hemolysis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased anion gap

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased serum chloride

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated serum albumin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elevated serum glucose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Elevated total bilirubin

explanation.summary: Serum LDH is a biomarker for hemolysis, but because LDH is widely expressed, the diagnosis requires correlative evidence such as elevated total bilirubin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mature erythrocytes are highly enriched with LDH because they depend on lactate formation for ATP production, so rupture of erythrocytes with release of cellular contents elevates serum LDH. However, LDH is expressed in many tissues and an elevated level can also indicate general tissue damage. A diagnosis of hemolysis therefore requires additional correlative evidence, such as elevated total bilirubin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A decreased anion gap reflects loss of unmeasured anions such as albumin, not erythrocyte rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chloride shifts relate to serum charge neutrality and do not indicate hemolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Albumin is a hepatic product and does not rise with erythrocyte destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serum glucose does not reflect erythrocyte rupture and does not corroborate hemolysis.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview I: General Reactions (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy from a region where food supplies are usually meager and of low quality is evaluated at a clinic. He has markedly decreased linear growth for his age and a decreased head circumference. There is no edema, and subcutaneous fat is preserved. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic malnutrition

choices.label: B
choices.text: Kwashiorkor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Marasmic kwashiorkor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Marasmus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Refeeding syndrome

explanation.summary: Chronic malnutrition is characterized by stunting (decreased linear growth) and decreased head circumference rather than edema or wasting.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic malnutrition describes unrelenting food deprivation in areas where food supplies are usually meager and food quality is low. It is characterized primarily by decreased linear growth (stunting) and decreased head circumference. It is less immediately deadly than acute malnutrition but still damaging to health.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Kwashiorkor is an acute malnutrition state whose distinguishing feature is edema, which is absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Marasmic kwashiorkor combines wasting and edema; neither is present in this child.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Marasmus is acute malnutrition with wasting and loss of subcutaneous fat, not preserved fat with stunting.
