questions.stem: A 2-year-old girl has an inherited deficiency of an enzyme that functions within the lysosome. Over time, undegraded material accumulates in her cells and produces progressive symptoms. Which of the following mechanisms best accounts for her disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cytosolic cytochrome c activating caspases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Defective peroxisomal catabolism of very long chain fatty acids

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dissipation of the proton gradient across the inner membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: Failed turnover of cellular constituents with accrual of waste

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced inner membrane surface area from loss of cristae

explanation.summary: Lysosomal storage diseases result from disrupted lysosomal enzyme function that prevents normal turnover of cellular constituents, causing waste to accrue.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lysosomal storage disease is a collection of more than 70 types of disorders that typically involve disruption of enzymatic function within the lysosome, which prevents normal turnover of cellular constituents. The resulting accrual of cellular waste accounts for many of the symptoms in this disease class.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytochrome c release initiates apoptosis rather than accumulation of cellular waste.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Defective peroxisomal fatty acid catabolism describes peroxisomal disorders such as Zellweger spectrum disorder, not a lysosomal enzyme deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Proton gradient dissipation describes uncoupling of OXPHOS, which is a mitochondrial process.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Loss of cristae would reduce OXPHOS capacity; it does not cause accumulation of undegraded material.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS

questions.stem: Two infants are diagnosed with different peroxisomal disorders. In one, the organelle fails to form; in the other, the organelle forms normally but a single degradative enzyme is nonfunctional. These two cases illustrate which pair of mechanisms that underlie peroxisomal disorders?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Defective biogenesis or loss of a selective catabolic enzyme

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess cytosolic NADPH production or loss of ribose 5-phosphate synthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of mitochondrial cristae or loss of functional ATP synthase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lysosomal enzyme deficiency or cytosolic waste accrual

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncoupling of OXPHOS or release of mitochondrial cytochrome c

explanation.summary: Peroxisomal disorders arise either from a lack of proper organelle formation (biogenesis) or from a lack of selective degradative enzymatic function.
explanation.whyCorrect: Peroxisomal disorders are a heterogeneous group of disorders caused by ineffective peroxisomal contribution to long chain fatty acid catabolism, either due to a lack of proper organelle formation (biogenesis) or a lack of selective degradative enzymatic function. The predominant example is Zellweger spectrum disorder.

whyWrongByChoice.B: NADPH and ribose production belong to the cytosolic pentose phosphate pathway, not the peroxisome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cristae and ATP synthase are mitochondrial structures unrelated to peroxisomal disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lysosomal enzyme deficiency with waste accrual describes lysosomal storage disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uncoupling and cytochrome c release are mitochondrial phenomena, not mechanisms of peroxisomal disease.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS

questions.stem: A medical student notes that, unlike the metabolism of carbohydrates and fats, one class of metabolic pathways is not localized to a single cellular space but collectively spans both the cytoplasm and the mitochondria. Which class of pathways is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amino acid catabolism and synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glycogen degradation and debranching

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycogen synthesis and branching

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glycolysis and pyruvate generation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pentose phosphate pathway and NADPH supply

explanation.summary: The catabolic and synthetic cascades of amino acids collectively encompass both the cytoplasm and mitochondria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike carbohydrates and fats, the catabolic and synthetic cascades of amino acids are not simply localized to a singular cellular space. Collectively these pathways encompass both the cytoplasm and mitochondria, reflecting the distinct and diverse chemistry contained within their chains.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Glycogen degradation occurs in the cytosol.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycogen synthesis occurs in the cytosol.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glycolysis is localized to the cytosol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pentose phosphate pathway is a cytosolic shunt of glycolysis.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS

questions.stem: An electron micrograph of a hepatocyte mitochondrion shows long, folded projections extending into the organelle's central lumen. These cristae are invaginations of which membrane, and into which space do they protrude?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inner membrane, protruding into the cytosol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inner membrane, protruding into the intermembrane space

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inner membrane, protruding into the matrix

choices.label: D
choices.text: Outer membrane, protruding into the cytosol

choices.label: E
choices.text: Outer membrane, protruding into the intermembrane space

explanation.summary: Cristae are long invaginations of the inner mitochondrial membrane that protrude into the matrix.
explanation.whyCorrect: The inner and outer mitochondrial membranes subdivide the mitochondrion into two spaces: the intermembrane space between the two membranes and the matrix, the lumen surrounded by the inner membrane. The inner membrane has long invaginations that protrude into the matrix known as cristae, and the ETC complexes and ATP synthase are embedded within this inner membrane.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The inner membrane is enclosed by the outer membrane and does not contact the cytosol.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cristae extend inward into the matrix, not outward into the intermembrane space.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cristae are formed by the inner membrane, not the outer membrane, and they do not extend into the cytosol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The outer membrane does not form cristae.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS

questions.stem: During a prolonged fast, skeletal muscle releases alanine, which is taken up by hepatocytes. Which of the following best describes the effect of alanine on hepatic glycolysis and its metabolic fate in the liver?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhibits glycolysis; is oxidized directly to acetyl-CoA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibits glycolysis; supplies pyruvate for gluconeogenesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: No effect on glycolysis; enters the pentose phosphate pathway

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stimulates glycolysis; regenerates NAD+ for glycolysis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stimulates glycolysis; serves as a glycolytic substrate

explanation.summary: Alanine is a negative regulator of hepatic glycolysis and a source of pyruvate for gluconeogenesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the liver, alanine is listed among the negative regulators of glycolysis, alongside glucagon and a high ATP/ADP ratio. At the same time, pyruvate derived from sources such as alanine and lactate is a substrate for gluconeogenesis, so alanine steers hepatic metabolism toward glucose production during fasting.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Although alanine inhibits glycolysis, the brick describes alanine as a source of pyruvate for gluconeogenesis, not as a molecule oxidized directly to acetyl-CoA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Alanine does inhibit hepatic glycolysis, and the pentose phosphate pathway uses glycolytic intermediates such as glucose 6-phosphate, not alanine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Alanine does not stimulate glycolysis; NAD+ regeneration during anaerobic glycolysis occurs through lactate formation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Alanine inhibits rather than stimulates hepatic glycolysis, and glucose (not alanine) is the glycolytic substrate.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman has not eaten for 18 hours, and her plasma glucagon concentration is elevated while insulin is low. Which of the following correctly describes the hormonal regulation of glycolysis and gluconeogenesis in her liver?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glucagon inhibits gluconeogenesis and stimulates glycolysis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucagon stimulates both glycolysis and gluconeogenesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucagon stimulates gluconeogenesis and inhibits glycolysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insulin inhibits both glycolysis and gluconeogenesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Insulin stimulates gluconeogenesis and inhibits glycolysis

explanation.summary: In the liver, glucagon activates gluconeogenesis and inhibits glycolysis, while insulin does the opposite.
explanation.whyCorrect: The major hepatic regulators of glycolysis are insulin (+) and glucagon (-), whereas for gluconeogenesis they are insulin (-) and glucagon (+). This reciprocal regulation ensures that biological parameters such as blood glucose concentration are properly maintained: during fasting, elevated glucagon drives glucose production while suppressing glucose consumption.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This reverses glucagon's actions; glucagon stimulates gluconeogenesis and inhibits glycolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glucagon inhibits hepatic glycolysis; it does not stimulate both pathways simultaneously.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Insulin is a positive regulator of glycolysis; it inhibits only gluconeogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Insulin has the opposite pattern: it stimulates glycolysis and inhibits gluconeogenesis.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS

questions.stem: A 26-year-old competitive mixed martial arts athlete is brought to the emergency department after collapsing during training. He had complained of fatigue, shortness of breath, and profuse sweating. He is hypertensive and hyperthermic (39.9 C / 103.9 F). Initial labs show no evidence of infection. His trainer reports the patient had been taking an unlabeled black-market substance to rapidly cut weight before a fight. Which of the following best explains the mechanism responsible for his hyperthermia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blockade of proton flow through ATP synthase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dissipation of the proton gradient

choices.label: C
choices.text: Impaired binding of oxygen to hemoglobin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of complex I preventing NADH oxidation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of cytochrome c oxidase at complex IV

explanation.summary: Chemical uncouplers such as 2,4-dinitrophenol (DNP) provide an alternate route for protons to re-enter the matrix, so electron transport chain activity yields heat instead of ATP.
explanation.whyCorrect: The presentation (black-market weight-loss agent, hyperthermia, diaphoresis, tachypnea) is classic for an unnatural uncoupler like DNP. Uncouplers let protons bypass ATP synthase, so the energy of the ETC combustion reaction is released as non-shivering thermogenesis rather than being captured as ATP. There is no safe dose and no antidote.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oligomycin blocks ATP synthase but does not create an alternate proton path, so it does not drive thermogenesis in this way.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Impaired hemoglobin-oxygen binding describes carbon monoxide's primary concern, not an uncoupler.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Complex I inhibition (rotenone) blocks electron flow and causes NADH accumulation rather than uncoupling-driven heat production.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Complex IV inhibition (cyanide, CO) blocks electron flow and oxygen consumption; it is not the hallmark heat-producing lesion and would not fit an uncoupling weight-loss agent.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man and a 40-year-old woman are both found unresponsive in a garage where a gasoline generator had been running. Both have a headache, confusion, and a reddish skin discoloration. Laboratory studies show a high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Carbon monoxide, like cyanide, inhibits which of the following components of oxidative phosphorylation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ATP synthase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coenzyme Q

choices.label: C
choices.text: Complex I

choices.label: D
choices.text: Complex III

choices.label: E
choices.text: Complex IV

explanation.summary: Both cyanide and carbon monoxide inhibit complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase) of the electron transport chain.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists both CN and CO as complex IV inhibitors. Blocking complex IV terminates electron transfer regardless of whether electrons entered via complex I or complex II, halting oxygen consumption and producing an anion gap metabolic acidosis with elevated lactate. For CO, the additional alteration of hemoglobin-oxygen binding is the primary clinical concern.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP synthase is inhibited by oligomycin, not by CN or CO.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coenzyme Q is a mobile carrier, not the target of these inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Complex I is the target of rotenone, not CN or CO.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Complex III is inhibited by antimycin A, not by CN or CO.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A full-term newborn is placed under a radiant warmer shortly after delivery. Rather than shivering, the infant maintains core temperature through non-shivering thermogenesis using reserves of specialized tissue enriched with mitochondria located around the neck, shoulders, and kidneys. Which of the following proteins is most directly responsible for the heat production in this tissue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ATP synthase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cytochrome c oxidase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Myoglobin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Succinate dehydrogenase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncoupling protein-1

explanation.summary: Brown adipose tissue generates heat through the natural uncoupler UCP-1, which transports protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane apart from ATP synthase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uncoupling proteins are proton transporters expressed in specialized tissues such as brown adipose tissue (BAT). BAT is most abundant in newborns and allows non-shivering thermogenesis after birth. Because protons return to the matrix through UCP-1 rather than ATP synthase, the energy is released as heat.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP synthase couples the proton gradient to ATP formation; its normal action does not produce the uncoupling-driven heat.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV) transfers electrons to oxygen but is not the proton leak channel responsible for thermogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Myoglobin stores oxygen in muscle and has no role in mitochondrial uncoupling.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Succinate dehydrogenase (complex II) feeds electrons into the chain and does not generate heat by uncoupling.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after ingesting a large quantity of aspirin. She is tachypneic, diaphoretic, and febrile without any source of infection. Which of the following mechanisms, shared with agents like 2,4-dinitrophenol, best accounts for the hyperthermia seen with high-dose salicylate exposure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blockade of coenzyme Q diffusion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enhanced coupling of the ETC to ATP synthase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibition of electron flow at complex III

choices.label: D
choices.text: Irreversible inhibition of complex IV

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation

explanation.summary: At high doses aspirin acts as an uncoupling agent, diffusing across the mitochondrial membrane to dissipate the proton gradient apart from ATP synthase.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick notes that aspirin at high doses functions much like DNP: it can diffuse across the mitochondrial membrane and act as a proton shuttle. Dissipating the gradient independently of ATP synthase releases energy as heat, explaining the hyperthermia and diaphoresis, and partly accounts for salicylate's adverse impact at high doses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blocking coenzyme Q diffusion inhibits the ETC and produces ROS, not uncoupling-driven thermogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Enhanced coupling would increase ATP yield and would not generate excess heat.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Complex III inhibition is the mechanism of antimycin A, not salicylate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Complex IV inhibition describes cyanide/CO and blocks oxygen consumption rather than uncoupling.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 38-year-old firefighter is pulled from a burning building filled with smoke from burning plastics. He is confused and hypotensive with a cherry-red skin discoloration. Arterial blood shows a high anion gap metabolic acidosis with a serum lactate of 11 mmol/L (reference 0.5-2.2). Which of the following best describes the underlying molecular mechanism of his poisoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deficient oxygen delivery from an uncorrected congenital heart defect

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibition of complex I preventing NADH oxidation by coenzyme Q

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibition of complex IV preventing tissue oxygen consumption

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced hemoglobin synthesis limiting systemic oxygen carriage

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncoupling of the proton gradient from ATP synthase, releasing heat

explanation.summary: Inhalation of HCN from a structural fire causes cyanide poisoning by inhibiting complex IV, so tissues cannot consume oxygen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyanide inhibits complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase), preventing the terminal step of the ETC and blocking cellular oxygen consumption. Because oxygen is delivered but not extracted, hemoglobin remains oxygenated, giving cherry-red skin. Anaerobic metabolism drives the profoundly elevated lactate (>8) and anion gap acidosis used to make the clinical diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A congenital heart defect causes cyanosis from poor perfusion, not the ETC blockade described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complex I inhibition (rotenone) is not the smoke-inhalation poison and would not classically give cherry-red skin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reduced hemoglobin synthesis causes cyanosis, a distinct entity from cyanide poisoning.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uncouplers cause hyperthermia and increased O2 consumption, not the blocked oxygen use seen here.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A patient with confirmed cyanide toxicity from a structural fire is being managed in the emergency department. Which of the following is the gold-standard treatment, acting by coordinating cyanide to cobalt so it can be excreted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activated charcoal alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deferoxamine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hydroxocobalamin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Methylene blue

choices.label: E
choices.text: N-acetylcysteine

explanation.summary: Hydroxocobalamin, a form of vitamin B12, is the preferred treatment for cyanide poisoning.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hydroxocobalamin is rapidly converted to cyanocobalamin as cyanide coordinates to the cobalt within the vitamin B12 structure. Because vitamin B12 is water soluble, the innocuous cyanocobalamin is then excreted. It is preferred over the amyl nitrite/sodium nitrite/sodium thiosulfate combination, which has more adverse effects.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Activated charcoal is a supportive measure for some ingestions but is not the specific antidote for cyanide.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Deferoxamine chelates iron and is used for iron overload/toxicity, not cyanide.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methylene blue treats methemoglobinemia, not cyanide toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: N-acetylcysteine is used for acetaminophen toxicity, not cyanide.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A patient with cyanide poisoning is noted to have a cherry-red skin discoloration rather than the blue-tinted skin expected with hypoxia. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cyanide causes methemoglobinemia, producing a red pigment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cyanide directly binds hemoglobin and turns it red

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cyanide increases hemoglobin synthesis, raising oxygen-carrying capacity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cyanide shifts hemoglobin to a low-affinity state, releasing oxygen to tissues

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tissues cannot consume oxygen, so hemoglobin remains oxygenated in the periphery

explanation.summary: By blocking complex IV, cyanide prevents tissues from consuming oxygen, so hemoglobin stays oxygenated and the skin appears cherry red.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyanide inhibits the electron transport chain at complex IV, so peripheral tissues cannot extract and consume oxygen. This interferes with the normal dissociation of oxygen from hemoglobin, leaving hemoglobin persistently oxygenated in the periphery, which produces the characteristic cherry-red discoloration (though not all cases show it).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Methemoglobinemia causes a chocolate-brown, not cherry-red, appearance and is not the mechanism here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The red color is from oxygenated hemoglobin, not from cyanide binding hemoglobin directly.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cyanide does not increase hemoglobin synthesis; the color reflects retained oxygenation, not more hemoglobin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cyanide does not act on hemoglobin oxygen affinity; the defect is in tissue oxygen utilization.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 2-month-old infant with a congenital heart defect has blue-tinted discoloration of the lips, fingers, and nailbeds. Which of the following best describes the mechanism underlying this cyanosis, distinguishing it from cyanide poisoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accumulation of oxygenated hemoglobin in the periphery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complex IV inhibition preventing tissue oxygen consumption

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inadequate delivery of oxygenated hemoglobin to peripheral tissues

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reactive oxygen species destroying peripheral capillaries

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation generating heat

explanation.summary: Cyanosis results from too little oxygenated hemoglobin reaching the tissues, producing deoxygenated (blue) blood in the systemic circulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyanosis is blue-tinted skin caused by deoxygenated blood in the systemic circulation, with the common mechanism being a general lack of oxygenated hemoglobin supplied to tissue. Causes span congenital heart defects that impair perfusion, genetic defects that impair oxygen binding, and reduced hemoglobin synthesis. This differs fundamentally from cyanide poisoning, where oxygen is present but cannot be consumed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Accumulation of oxygenated hemoglobin would give a red appearance, the opposite of cyanosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complex IV inhibition describes cyanide poisoning, in which hemoglobin stays oxygenated (cherry red), not blue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ROS-mediated capillary destruction is not the described mechanism of cyanosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uncoupling produces heat and does not explain blue skin discoloration.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A researcher exposes cultured cells to an agent that blocks the entry of electrons from NADH into the electron transport chain while leaving complex II intact. Which of the following agents would most greatly increase the intracellular NADH/NAD+ ratio?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A complex I inhibitor such as rotenone

choices.label: B
choices.text: A complex II inhibitor

choices.label: C
choices.text: A natural uncoupler such as UCP-1

choices.label: D
choices.text: An ATP synthase inhibitor acting only on complex V

choices.label: E
choices.text: An unnatural uncoupler such as DNP

explanation.summary: Complex I oxidizes NADH; inhibiting it causes NADH to accumulate, raising the NADH/NAD+ ratio.
explanation.whyCorrect: Complex I accepts electrons from NADH and shuttles them to coenzyme Q. Inhibiting complex I (e.g., rotenone) prevents NADH oxidation, so reduced NADH accumulates and the NADH/NAD+ ratio rises, promoting lactate formation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Complex II oxidizes FADH2, not NADH; inhibiting it would still allow NADH to be oxidized via complex I.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A natural uncoupler likewise speeds electron flow and NADH oxidation, so it would not raise the ratio the most.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ATP synthase inhibition slows the chain indirectly but does not selectively block NADH oxidation the way complex I inhibition does.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uncouplers augment the ETC and tend to increase oxidation of NADH to NAD+, lowering rather than raising the ratio.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: An experimental therapeutic drug shows unexpected cellular toxicity because of an off-target effect: it binds and prevents the free diffusion of coenzyme Q within the mitochondrial inner membrane. Which of the following best accounts for the cellular injury caused by this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A primary lack of oxygen supply to the cell

choices.label: B
choices.text: ATP depletion together with reactive oxygen species

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excess ATP production driving oxidative damage

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased proton pumping across the inner membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Non-shivering thermogenesis overheating the cell

explanation.summary: Blocking coenzyme Q behaves like an ETC inhibitor: electrons from NADH and FADH2 cannot pass forward, halting proton pumping and ATP synthesis while generating damaging ROS.
explanation.whyCorrect: Without the lipid-soluble carrier CoQ, electrons from complex I and complex II cannot move forward, so proton pumping and ATP synthesis fall. Impeded electron flow also generates ROS from inefficient electron transfer, and cells shift to lactate formation. The combination of ATP depletion and ROS accounts for the toxicity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oxygen is still supplied; the problem is that it cannot be consumed, so this is a lack of oxygen consumption, not supply.
whyWrongByChoice.C: ATP is depleted, not overproduced, when the ETC is blocked.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blocking electron flow reduces, rather than increases, proton pumping.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thermogenesis is a hallmark of uncouplers; interfering with CoQ describes an inhibitor, not an uncoupler.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A patient with severe electron transport chain inhibition develops a rapidly rising serum lactate and a high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Which of the following best explains why lactate accumulates in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased mitochondrial oxygen consumption oxidizes lactate more slowly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lactate is produced by complex IV as a direct byproduct of oxygen reduction to water

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pyruvate is reduced to lactate to regenerate NAD+ so glycolysis can continue

choices.label: D
choices.text: The inhibited ETC directly converts accumulated pyruvate to lactate in the matrix

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncoupling proteins convert cytosolic pyruvate to lactate to release heat

explanation.summary: When the ETC is blocked, cells reduce pyruvate to lactate to regenerate NAD+, sustaining some ATP production from glycolysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: ETC inhibition causes NADH to accumulate because it can no longer be oxidized. To keep glycolysis running and salvage some substrate-level ATP, pyruvate is reduced to lactate, regenerating NAD+ from NADH. This drives the rapid lactate rise and anion gap metabolic acidosis seen with OXPHOS inhibitors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oxygen consumption falls, not rises, with ETC inhibition, and this does not explain lactate generation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complex IV reduces oxygen to water; it does not generate lactate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The ETC does not convert pyruvate to lactate; lactate dehydrogenase does so in the cytosol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uncoupling proteins transport protons for thermogenesis and do not produce lactate from pyruvate.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A pharmacology student compares two poisons: one that renders complex I completely inoperable and another that renders complex IV completely inoperable, assuming FADH2 substrates remain available. Which of the following best explains why complex IV inhibition halts electron transport more completely than complex I inhibition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complex I inhibition prevents complex II from receiving electrons from FADH2

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complex I is the only entry point for all electrons into the electron transport chain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Complex IV inhibition also uncouples the proton gradient from ATP synthase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Complex IV inhibition increases tissue oxygen consumption to compensate for the block

choices.label: E
choices.text: Complex IV is a required step for electrons from both complex I and complex II

explanation.summary: Because electrons from complex I and complex II both converge and must pass through complex IV, blocking complex IV stops all electron flow, while blocking complex I still allows complex II to contribute.
explanation.whyCorrect: Electrons from either complex I or complex II are shuttled by coenzyme Q into the shared downstream chain. If complex I is blocked but FADH2 substrates are present, complex II still feeds electrons in, preserving some diminished ATP production. Inhibiting complex IV blocks a step required by electrons from both complexes, effectively terminating electron transfer regardless of the reduced coenzyme considered.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Complex II receives electrons from FADH2 independently of complex I, so complex I inhibition does not cut off complex II.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complex I is not the only entry point; complex II (succinate dehydrogenase) provides a separate entry via FADH2.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Complex IV inhibition blocks electron flow; it does not act as an uncoupler of the proton gradient.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Complex IV inhibition decreases, rather than increases, oxygen consumption.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 3-day-old infant maintains body temperature after exposure to a cool room without any visible muscle activity. A first-year student asks how this heat is produced. Which of the following best distinguishes the infant's non-shivering thermogenesis from shivering?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It depends on increased ATP synthesis by ATP synthase in skeletal muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: It depends on inhibition of electron flow at complex IV of the respiratory chain

choices.label: C
choices.text: It depends on mitochondrial metabolism rather than involuntary muscle contraction

choices.label: D
choices.text: It depends on rapid involuntary contraction of skeletal muscle rather than on mitochondria

choices.label: E
choices.text: It depends on reduced oxygen consumption by mitochondria in brown adipose tissue

explanation.summary: Non-shivering thermogenesis is heat generated by mitochondrial metabolism through uncoupling, not by muscle contraction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Shivering produces heat from rapid, involuntary muscle contraction. Non-shivering thermogenesis does not require muscle contraction; instead, uncoupling proteins in brown adipose tissue let electron transport chain activity yield heat instead of ATP, as the combustion reaction (carbon source + O2 -> H2O + CO2 + energy) must still be completed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Uncoupling diverts protons away from ATP synthase, lowering rather than raising ATP synthesis from OXPHOS.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complex IV inhibition is the mechanism of cyanide and carbon monoxide, not of physiologic heat production.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rapid involuntary muscle contraction describes shivering, the process being contrasted.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uncouplers do not inhibit the ETC; electron flow and oxygen consumption continue as the energy is released as heat.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A biochemist studies how 2,4-dinitrophenol moves protons across the mitochondrial inner membrane. Which of the following sequences best describes the behavior of this agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds ATP synthase and forces protons through the enzyme without ATP formation

choices.label: B
choices.text: It inserts into the inner membrane as a fixed pore that passes protons into the matrix

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is protonated in the intermembrane space, diffuses across the membrane, and is deprotonated in the matrix

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is protonated in the matrix, diffuses outward, and releases protons into the intermembrane space

choices.label: E
choices.text: It transfers electrons from coenzyme Q directly to oxygen, bypassing proton pumping

explanation.summary: Unnatural uncouplers are lipid-soluble molecules that bind and release protons, shuttling them from the proton-rich intermembrane space into the matrix apart from ATP synthase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chemical uncouplers such as DNP are lipid soluble, allowing them to diffuse freely into the intermembrane space, where they become protonated in the proton-rich environment. They then freely diffuse across the mitochondrial inner membrane and become deprotonated within the matrix, dissipating the gradient without passing through ATP synthase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DNP provides a proton route apart from ATP synthase; it does not act through the enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Membrane-spanning proton transport describes uncoupling proteins (UCPs); DNP is a freely diffusible chemical, not an anchored pore.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The direction is reversed; protons are picked up where they are abundant (intermembrane space) and released in the matrix.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DNP does not carry electrons; it carries protons, and it does not alter the electron path.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 31-year-old bodybuilder has been taking illicit 2,4-dinitrophenol capsules for 2 weeks and reports rapid fat loss along with sweating and heat intolerance. Which of the following best explains the accelerated loss of adipose tissue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A falling ADP:ATP ratio suppresses lipid storage and promotes release from adipocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: A rising ADP:ATP ratio drives oxidation of mobilized lipids to generate more reduced coenzymes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blockade of ATP synthase by DNP prevents fatty acid synthesis from acetyl-CoA within the cytosol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Direct binding of DNP to adipocyte lipid droplets releases stored fatty acids into plasma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of complex I by DNP forces mobilized lipids to be excreted rather than oxidized

explanation.summary: Unnatural uncouplers increase catabolism: as the ADP:ATP ratio rises, the body oxidizes mobilized carbon sources such as lipids in a futile attempt to restore ATP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unnatural uncouplers produce a general mobilization of carbon sources from metabolic pathways in a futile attempt to remedy the ATP decrement. As the ADP:ATP ratio increases, the body oxidizes mobilized carbon sources (e.g., lipids) to produce more reduced coenzymes so the ETC can pump additional protons. This aggressive promotion of fat catabolism is why agents like DNP were pursued for weight loss.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Uncoupling lowers ATP, so the ADP:ATP ratio rises rather than falls.
whyWrongByChoice.C: ATP synthase blockade describes oligomycin, and the effect of DNP is enhanced oxidative catabolism, not impaired synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: DNP acts as a proton shuttle across the mitochondrial inner membrane; it does not act on lipid droplets directly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DNP is an uncoupler, not a complex I inhibitor, and lipids are oxidized, not excreted.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman undergoes imaging that identifies metabolically active adipose depots. Compared with white adipose tissue, which of the following best describes the distribution of brown fat in an adult human?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone marrow of the long bones and the flat bones of the pelvis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Omental and mesenteric fat surrounding the intestines and liver

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pericardial and epicardial fat surrounding the heart and great vessels

choices.label: D
choices.text: Shoulders and neck, around the vertebrae, and over the kidneys

choices.label: E
choices.text: Subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen, buttocks, and thighs

explanation.summary: Brown fat is localized to the shoulders and neck, around the vertebrae, and over the kidneys, a pattern very different from the subcutaneous and abdominal distribution of white fat.
explanation.whyCorrect: In humans, brown fat decreases with age and is located in the shoulders and neck, around the vertebrae, and over the kidneys. These sites are strategically localized to maximize protection and generate heat upon cold exposure. Its brown color comes from the highly enriched mitochondria expressing UCP.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow is not a described location of brown adipose tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Abdominal (visceral) fat is characteristic of white adipose tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pericardial fat is not among the brown fat sites described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Subcutaneous and abdominal fat is the distribution of white adipose tissue, not brown fat.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A wildlife physiologist notes that a hibernating bear maintains body warmth for months while performing almost no physical activity. Which of the following features of the bear's adipose tissue best accounts for this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abundant brown fat that generates heat while requiring minimal ATP

choices.label: B
choices.text: Abundant white fat that stores ATP for release during sleep

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated complex IV activity that increases oxygen consumption

choices.label: D
choices.text: High ATP synthase activity that converts stored fat into ATP

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced mitochondrial density that limits heat loss

explanation.summary: Hibernating animals have even more brown fat than human newborns, providing warmth during winter sleep when ATP demand is minimal.
explanation.whyCorrect: Brown fat is most abundant in human newborns but is even more abundant in hibernating animals like bears, who need to stay warm during their winter sleep but need minimal ATP as they sleep. UCP-expressing mitochondria in brown adipose tissue release the energy of the ETC as heat rather than capturing it as ATP.

whyWrongByChoice.B: White fat does not store ATP, and the tissue supporting hibernation warmth is brown fat.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Heat comes from uncoupling via UCPs, not from an inhibitor- or complex IV-specific change.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The point of hibernation thermogenesis is heat production with minimal ATP need, not high ATP synthase output.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Brown fat is enriched with mitochondria; that abundance is what accounts for its heat output and coloring.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A patient who ingested a black-market slimming agent develops severe hyperthermia with hepatic and cerebral dysfunction, whereas a cold-exposed newborn generating heat through brown adipose tissue never develops organ injury. Which of the following best explains why the chemical agent, unlike the physiologic uncoupler, damages organs such as the brain and liver?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It generates reactive oxygen species by blocking electron flow at complex III of the respiratory chain

choices.label: B
choices.text: It increases ATP synthesis by ATP synthase to a level that overheats brain and liver tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is expressed only in brain and liver mitochondria, which tolerate heat poorly

choices.label: D
choices.text: It requires metabolic activation by hepatic enzymes before it can act on mitochondria

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its abundance is determined by intake rather than by tissue-specific, regulated gene expression

explanation.summary: Unnatural uncouplers are not governed by tissue-specific gene expression; their abundance depends on intake, so they uncouple gradients indiscriminately in organs ill equipped for elevated temperatures.
explanation.whyCorrect: UCP expression is restricted to specialized tissues like BAT and is tightly regulated to ensure temperature balance (it can be turned on and off). In contrast, agents like DNP have a much broader tissue distribution, their abundance is determined by intake or exposure, and they accumulate in an unregulated manner to fully collapse gradients. This generates heat in organs such as the brain or liver that cannot maintain function at elevated temperatures, compromising organ function to the point of death.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Uncouplers do not block electron flow or generate ROS; that is the hallmark of ETC inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Uncouplers decrease ATP production from OXPHOS; the heat comes from energy not captured as ATP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DNP is a chemical that is not expressed at all; it distributes broadly wherever it is taken in.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metabolic activation is a feature of methanol-derived formic acid, not of DNP.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 3 hours after ingesting several 2,4-dinitrophenol capsules. He is hyperthermic (40.5 C), tachycardic, tachypneic, diaphoretic, and confused. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intravenous hydroxocobalamin 5 g infused over 15 minutes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intravenous methylene blue 1 mg/kg over 5 minutes, repeated once

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral N-acetylcysteine 140 mg/kg loading dose, then maintenance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Physical cooling, activated charcoal, and supportive ventilation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sodium nitrite followed by intravenous sodium thiosulfate

explanation.summary: There is no antidote for DNP; treatment is limited to supportive care for the symptoms present.
explanation.whyCorrect: The presentation (hyperthermia apart from infection, tachypnea, tachycardia, diaphoresis, altered mental state after an illicit slimming agent) is DNP toxicity. Unfortunately, there is no antidote, and treatments are greatly limited to supportive care. Typical protocols can include physical cooling of the patient, activated charcoal, mechanical ventilation, and other appropriate intravenous solutions and supplements.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hydroxocobalamin is the gold-standard antidote for cyanide, which inhibits complex IV; it does not reverse uncoupling.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Methylene blue is used for methemoglobinemia and has no role in uncoupler poisoning.
whyWrongByChoice.C: N-acetylcysteine treats acetaminophen toxicity, not uncoupler ingestion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The nitrite/thiosulfate combination is an alternative cyanide regimen, not a treatment for DNP.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with massive 2,4-dinitrophenol ingestion initially has a heart rate of 140/min. Over the next several hours, despite aggressive cooling, her heart rate falls to 38/min and she becomes hypotensive and apneic. Which of the following best explains the transition in her heart rate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accumulated reactive oxygen species have destroyed the pacemaker cells of the sinoatrial node

choices.label: B
choices.text: ATP within cardiac cells has been exhausted so contractile processes are no longer viable

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cooling has reversed the uncoupling and restored a normal resting sinus rhythm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excess ATP from increased catabolism has suppressed sinoatrial pacemaker activity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hemoglobin can no longer release its bound oxygen to metabolically active cardiac tissue

explanation.summary: The metabolic surge caused by DNP is only an initial response; once ATP is insufficient, flux slows across all pathways, and tachycardia transitions to bradycardia as ATP is exhausted in cardiac cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The increase in metabolic activity is an initial response to agents like DNP. Once ATP levels are insufficient for the maintenance of normal processes (e.g., breathing), metabolic flux slows across all pathways, lactate rapidly increases, and as more processes become non-viable due to lack of ATP, death occurs. Tachycardia is an initial symptom, but with a severe dose it eventually transitions to bradycardia as ATP is exhausted within the cardiac cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ROS generation is a hallmark of ETC inhibitors, not uncouplers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cooling is supportive only; there is no antidote, and a heart rate of 38/min with apnea is decompensation, not recovery.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased catabolism fails to rescue ATP when enough uncoupler is present; ATP is depleted, not in excess.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Persistent oxygenation of hemoglobin describes cyanide poisoning; DNP does not alter oxygen release.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A researcher measures oxygen consumption in two suspensions of freshly isolated mitochondria supplied with substrate. Suspension 1 receives 2,4-dinitrophenol and suspension 2 receives rotenone. Compared with untreated controls, which of the following best describes the immediate change in oxygen consumption?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Suspension 1 decreases; suspension 2 decreases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Suspension 1 decreases; suspension 2 increases

choices.label: C
choices.text: Suspension 1 increases; suspension 2 decreases

choices.label: D
choices.text: Suspension 1 increases; suspension 2 increases

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suspension 1 unchanged; suspension 2 decreases

explanation.summary: Uncouplers initially increase oxygen consumption because electron transport speeds up, whereas ETC inhibitors decrease oxygen consumption from the start of exposure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uncoupling agents increase the rate of oxidative catabolism to sustain the rapidly diffusing proton gradient, so the rate of oxygen consumption increases concomitantly as electron transport occurs at a more rapid rate initially. In contrast, ETC inhibitors such as rotenone (complex I) prevent the flow of electrons and oxygen consumption from the start of exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Uncouplers do not inhibit the ETC; oxygen consumption rises rather than falls with DNP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This reverses both agents; inhibitors block electron flow and oxygen use, uncouplers accelerate them.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rotenone blocks electron flow into the chain and therefore reduces oxygen consumption.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DNP changes oxygen consumption; it accelerates electron flow rather than leaving it unchanged.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: Cultured hepatocytes are exposed to antimycin A, and flux through the TCA cycle is measured. Which of the following best explains the change in TCA cycle activity observed after exposure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased flux, because accumulated NADH and FADH2 are no longer oxidized by the ETC

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased flux, because protons leak back into the matrix apart from ATP synthase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased flux, because complex III inhibition raises NAD+ availability

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased flux, because the cell mobilizes carbon sources to restore ATP

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unchanged flux, because the TCA cycle is independent of the ETC

explanation.summary: ETC inhibitors decrease flux through upstream metabolic pathways such as the TCA cycle because reduced NADH and FADH2 accumulate and are no longer oxidized.
explanation.whyCorrect: In contrast to uncouplers, ETC inhibitors prevent the flow of electrons and oxygen consumption from the start of exposure, decreasing the flux through upstream metabolic pathways (e.g., TCA cycle). This is largely due to the accumulation of reduced NADH and FADH2 that is no longer oxidized by the inhibited ETC. Antimycin A blocks complex III.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Proton leak apart from ATP synthase describes uncoupling; antimycin A is an inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibition prevents NADH oxidation, so NAD+ becomes scarce rather than abundant.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mobilization of carbon sources and enhanced catabolism is the response to uncouplers, not to inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The TCA cycle depends on the ETC to regenerate NAD+ and FAD, so it slows when the chain is blocked.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man has a coronary artery occlusion that is opened by catheter intervention 90 minutes after symptom onset. Myocardial injury is found to extend beyond what oxygen and ATP deprivation alone would explain. Which of the following best accounts for the additional injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A burst of reactive oxygen species generated when electron flow resumes after restored oxygen delivery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess ATP synthesis by the restored proton gradient that overloads the myocardium after reperfusion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Irreversible inhibition of complex IV by cyanide released locally from the ischemic myocardium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Persistent lack of oxygen substrate at complex IV despite restored coronary blood flow

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncoupling of the inner mitochondrial proton gradient by lactate accumulating during the ischemic period

explanation.summary: Temporary inhibition of the ETC followed by restoration of flow, as in ischemic reperfusion injury, produces bursts of ROS that exacerbate the damage from oxygen and ATP deprivation alone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ischemic reperfusion injury occurs when blood supply is temporarily occluded to a site, preventing delivery of O2 and depriving the ETC of a needed substrate to allow electron flow. If the impediment is removed and blood flow is restored, ROS are generated. This burst of ROS reacts with DNA, lipids, and proteins and exacerbates the damage caused by oxygen and ATP deprivation alone.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Reperfusion does not cause damaging ATP excess; the injury is ROS mediated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cyanide exposure comes from fires, nitroprusside, or cyanogenic foods, not from ischemic tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reperfusion restores oxygen delivery; the harm arises precisely because electron flow resumes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lactate accumulates during ETC blockade but is not an uncoupler of the proton gradient.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman receiving doxorubicin for breast cancer develops a progressive decline in cardiac output. Which of the following is the posited mechanism of this adverse effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conversion of the drug to formic acid, which irreversibly inhibits complex IV in cardiomyocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Depletion of the brown adipose tissue surrounding the heart, removing a thermogenic reserve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Generation of reactive oxygen species in myocardium as the drug inhibits electron transfer during OXPHOS

choices.label: D
choices.text: Persistent oxygenation of hemoglobin limiting oxygen release to the myocardium at the capillary level

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncoupling of OXPHOS in cardiomyocytes, dissipating the proton gradient and producing thermogenic injury

explanation.summary: Doxorubicin cardiotoxicity is attributed to ROS generated in myocardial tissue because the drug inhibits electron transfer during OXPHOS.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxorubicin, a bacterially derived compound used as cancer chemotherapy since the 1960s, has a common deleterious side effect of compromised cardiac output. While not fully proven, the posited source of cardiac damage is the generation of reactive oxygen species within myocardial tissue as doxorubicin inhibits electron transfer during OXPHOS. Inefficient electron transfer within the ETC generates ROS that damage DNA, lipids, and proteins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Formic acid arises from methanol catabolism, not from doxorubicin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Brown fat depletion is not a described mechanism of doxorubicin injury.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Persistent hemoglobin oxygenation is the mechanism of cherry-red skin in cyanide poisoning.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxorubicin is described as inhibiting electron transfer, not as an uncoupler; uncouplers do not generate ROS.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A research group engineers cells to overexpress an uncoupling protein and finds that markers of oxidative stress decrease. Which of the following best explains this protective effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The protein augments electron flow through the ETC, counteracting inefficient electron transfer

choices.label: B
choices.text: The protein blocks electron entry at complex I so that fewer electrons can escape and reduce oxygen

choices.label: C
choices.text: The protein coordinates reactive oxygen species to a cobalt center for renal excretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: The protein increases ATP synthesis, which powers repair of oxidized DNA and lipids

choices.label: E
choices.text: The protein reduces oxygen delivery to the mitochondria so that less superoxide forms

explanation.summary: UCPs are expressed not only for thermogenesis but also to reduce oxidative stress, because augmented electron flow counteracts the inefficient electron transfer that produces ROS.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uncoupling proteins are expressed in a variety of tissues to aid in thermogenesis as well as reducing oxidative stress. ROS are generated any time there is inefficient electron transfer within the ETC, as with inhibitors. In contrast, augmented electron flow, as is observed by the expression of UCPs, can be a protective measure that reduces or counteracts the oxidative stress associated with ROS.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blocking electron flow at complex I describes rotenone and would generate ROS rather than reduce it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coordination to cobalt describes how hydroxocobalamin detoxifies cyanide, not how UCPs work.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uncoupling lowers ATP production from OXPHOS; the protection comes from electron flow, not ATP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: UCPs increase, not decrease, oxygen consumption by accelerating the ETC.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A state wildlife agency uses a naturally derived plant-root compound to regulate fish populations in a lake. Workers handling the compound are told that accidental fatal poisoning is rare because it is poorly absorbed through the skin. Which of the following components of oxidative phosphorylation does this compound inhibit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ATP synthase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coenzyme Q

choices.label: C
choices.text: Complex I

choices.label: D
choices.text: Complex III

choices.label: E
choices.text: Complex IV

explanation.summary: Rotenone, a natural plant-root compound used as a pesticide and for fish population management, inhibits complex I.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rotenone is a natural compound derived from roots of select plants from Asia, South America, and East Africa. It is commonly used as a pesticide or by wildlife management to regulate fish populations. Deaths from accidental poisoning are rare because it is poorly absorbed through the skin. Its target is complex I.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP synthase is inhibited by oligomycin, a bacterial product used in metabolic research.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coenzyme Q is a mobile electron carrier and is not the described target of rotenone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Complex III is the target of antimycin A, a bacterial product used in fungicides and fishery management.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Complex IV is inhibited by cyanide, carbon monoxide, and formic acid.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: Several swimmers develop dizziness, fatigue, and altered mental status after using a recreational lake that had recently been treated with a bacterially produced fishery-management agent. Laboratory studies show a high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Which of the following is the most likely site of inhibition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ATP synthase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complex I

choices.label: C
choices.text: Complex II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Complex III

choices.label: E
choices.text: Complex IV

explanation.summary: Antimycin A, produced by bacteria and used in fungicides and fishery management, inhibits complex III; exposure usually arises occupationally or through treated water.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antimycin A is produced by bacteria and used in a variety of commercial applications such as fungicides and fishery management. Issues usually arise from occupational exposure or accidental exposure to treated water (e.g., recreational areas). It targets complex III, and like other OXPHOS inhibitors produces a high anion gap metabolic acidosis, dizziness, altered mental status, and fatigue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP synthase is targeted by oligomycin, which is used predominantly in metabolic research rather than fishery management.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complex I is the target of rotenone, a plant-root compound.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase) is not the target of any inhibitor in the summary chart.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Complex IV is targeted by cyanide, carbon monoxide, and formic acid, not by the fishery agent described.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with chronic kidney disease is treated for hypertensive crisis with a continuous infusion of a potent intravenous vasodilator. On the third day he becomes confused with a high anion gap metabolic acidosis and a serum lactate of 10 mmol/L. Which of the following best explains his deterioration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Formic acid from the drug has inhibited ATP synthase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nitroprusside has generated cyanide, which inhibits complex IV

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduced renal perfusion has decreased hemoglobin synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: The vasodilator has inhibited complex I in the brain

choices.label: E
choices.text: The vasodilator has uncoupled OXPHOS in hepatic mitochondria

explanation.summary: Nitroprusside can generate concerning levels of cyanide when prescribed for hypertensive crisis, especially in patients with compromised kidney function.
explanation.whyCorrect: The potent vasodilator nitroprusside can generate concerning levels of CN when prescribed for hypertensive crisis, especially in patients with compromised kidney function. Cyanide inhibits complex IV, preventing tissue oxygen consumption and producing altered mental status with an anion gap metabolic acidosis and a profoundly elevated lactate (>8 mmol/L), which is how the diagnosis is made clinically.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Formic acid derives from methanol and inhibits complex IV, not ATP synthase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reduced hemoglobin synthesis is a cause of cyanosis and does not produce a lactate of 10 mmol/L.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Complex I is the target of rotenone, not of cyanide released from nitroprusside.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nitroprusside toxicity is from cyanide, an ETC inhibitor, not from uncoupling.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man develops headache, nausea, anxiety, and confusion several hours after eating a large amount of improperly prepared cassava. There is no history of smoke exposure or medication use. Which of the following best describes the source and target of the toxin responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antimycin A from bacteria inhibiting complex III

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carbon monoxide from incomplete combustion inhibiting complex IV

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cyanide from a cyanogenic glycoside inhibiting complex IV

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oligomycin from bacteria inhibiting ATP synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rotenone from plant roots inhibiting complex I

explanation.summary: Select foods such as cassava and certain nuts contain cyanogenic glycosides that release cyanide, a complex IV inhibitor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although inhalation of HCN gas during structural fires is the most common route of exposure, cyanide toxicity can also occur through ingestion of cyanogenic glycosides; select food sources (e.g., cassava, select nuts) can be a source of CN. Cyanide inhibits complex IV. Nonspecific symptoms such as headaches and nausea are common, along with anxiety and altered mental status.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antimycin A exposure is occupational or from treated water, not from eating cassava.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbon monoxide comes from gas-fueled equipment, wood stoves, fires, and solvents, not from food.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oligomycin is a research reagent, not a food-borne toxin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rotenone is derived from plant roots used as pesticide or for fish control; it is not a dietary toxin from cassava.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A metabolic research laboratory adds a bacterial product to isolated mitochondria to study ATP synthase. Which of the following agents was most likely used?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2,4-Dinitrophenol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antimycin A

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hydroxocobalamin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oligomycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rotenone

explanation.summary: Oligomycin is a bacterial product used predominantly in metabolic research that inhibits ATP synthase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oligomycin is a bacterial product that is predominantly used in metabolic research studies, and its target is ATP synthase (complex V). Many of the agents in the inhibitor chart are commonly used in biomedical research labs to examine mitochondrial function.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DNP is a chemical uncoupler, not a bacterial product, and does not inhibit ATP synthase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antimycin A is bacterial but inhibits complex III, not ATP synthase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hydroxocobalamin is a manufactured form of vitamin B12 used to treat cyanide poisoning, not an OXPHOS inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rotenone is a plant-derived complex I inhibitor.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 37-year-old man drinks a windshield-washer fluid containing methanol. Over the next day he develops blurred vision, abdominal pain, and a high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Which of the following best explains why his symptoms emerge later and are more widespread than those of a localized bee sting, which delivers the same toxic molecule?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Methanol coordinates to the cobalt center of vitamin B12, delaying its renal excretion over several days

choices.label: B
choices.text: Methanol directly uncouples OXPHOS in every tissue and requires time to accumulate in brown adipose depots

choices.label: C
choices.text: Methanol inhibits complex I directly at the flavin mononucleotide site, and the delay reflects slow absorption through the skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Methanol is converted to cyanide, which binds hemoglobin and is cleared slowly by the kidneys over days

choices.label: E
choices.text: Methanol must be oxidatively catabolized to formic acid, which then inhibits complex IV systemically at high concentration

explanation.summary: Formic acid, produced by oxidative catabolism of ingested methanol, inhibits complex IV; unlike the chart inhibitors, methanol requires metabolic activation, and ingestion gives higher, more widespread concentrations than a localized bee sting.
explanation.whyCorrect: Formic acid derived from a bee sting or from ingestion and subsequent oxidative catabolism of methanol is an inhibitor of complex IV of the ETC, and many of its adverse symptoms are associated with interference with OXPHOS. While the bee sting is typically more localized, ingestion of a poison leading to formic acid formation is more widespread, with higher concentrations accounting for the greater symptom severity. The ETC inhibitors listed in the chart do not require metabolic activation or modification like methanol.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Coordination to cobalt in vitamin B12 is how hydroxocobalamin detoxifies cyanide, not a methanol pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Methanol-derived formic acid is an ETC inhibitor, not an uncoupler, and brown fat is unrelated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The target is complex IV (not complex I), and the delay reflects metabolic activation, not skin absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methanol is not converted to cyanide; it is catabolized to formic acid.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman is rescued from a house fire. On arrival she is anxious and hypertensive with tachycardia, dilated pupils, and a brief seizure. Cyanide toxicity is suspected. Which of the following best explains these early findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Depletion of ATP in cardiac and neural tissue from blocked oxidative phosphorylation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reactive oxygen species damaging the sinoatrial node and cortical neurons within minutes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reflex sympathetic response to persistent oxygenation of hemoglobin in the peripheral venous blood

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release of excitatory neurotransmitters in addition to complex IV binding

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thermogenesis from uncoupled OXPHOS in the brain and skeletal muscle raising core temperature

explanation.summary: In addition to complex IV inhibition, cyanide causes release of excitatory neurotransmitters, producing early hypertension, tachycardia, anxiety, seizures, and pupillary dilation before later depression.
explanation.whyCorrect: CN toxicity most commonly occurs through exposure to burning nitrogen compounds in fires. In addition to the effects of complex IV binding, CN also causes the release of excitatory neurotransmitters, so patients may present with hypertension, tachycardia, anxiety, seizures, and pupillary dilation. As symptoms advance, the profound inability to utilize oxygen results in depressed mental status, hypotension, and bradycardia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP depletion accounts for the later phase of depressed mental status, hypotension, and bradycardia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ROS contribute to cellular injury but are not the described cause of the early excitatory phase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Persistent hemoglobin oxygenation explains cherry-red skin, not the excitatory neurologic findings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cyanide is an ETC inhibitor, not an uncoupler, and does not produce thermogenesis.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A patient with clinically diagnosed cyanide poisoning is being treated at a rural facility that does not stock hydroxocobalamin. Which of the following is the most appropriate alternative regimen, and what is its principal drawback?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activated charcoal and aggressive physical cooling; no effect at all on tissue oxygen consumption

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amyl nitrite, sodium nitrite, and sodium thiosulfate; comparatively more adverse side effects

choices.label: C
choices.text: High-dose aspirin with bicarbonate; uncouples OXPHOS and causes dangerous hyperthermia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intravenous methylene blue; worsens hemoglobin oxygen binding and causes serotonin toxicity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral cyanocobalamin tablets; far too slow to coordinate cyanide in the circulation

explanation.summary: The combination of amyl nitrite, sodium nitrite, and sodium thiosulfate is an alternative cyanide treatment used only when hydroxocobalamin is unavailable because it has more adverse side effects.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hydroxocobalamin is the gold-standard treatment for CN poisoning. Other treatments exist (e.g., the combination of amyl nitrite, sodium nitrite, and sodium thiosulfate) but comparatively have more adverse side effects and are only used when hydroxocobalamin is not available.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cooling and charcoal are the supportive protocol for DNP, which has no antidote; cyanide does have specific antidotes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: High-dose aspirin is itself an uncoupler with adverse effects and has no role in cyanide treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methylene blue is not a cyanide antidote described here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cyanocobalamin is the innocuous excreted product formed after hydroxocobalamin coordinates cyanide, not a treatment.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 6-month-old boy has persistent blue discoloration of the lips and nailbeds. Echocardiography shows a structurally normal heart with normal tissue perfusion, and pulmonary function is normal. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism of his cyanosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A congenital cardiac defect impairing perfusion of peripheral tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: A genetic alteration that prevents effective oxygen binding to hemoglobin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excess oxygenated hemoglobin retained in the peripheral venous circulation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of complex IV preventing oxygen consumption by the tissues

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncoupling of OXPHOS in the brown adipose tissue of the neck and shoulders

explanation.summary: Cyanosis has a spectrum of causes; when perfusion is normal, genetic alterations that prevent effective oxygen binding to hemoglobin or a decrement in hemoglobin synthesis can leave tissues short of oxygenated hemoglobin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Deoxygenated blood in the systemic circulation causes cyanosis, a blue-tinted skin most noticeable in lips, fingers, toes, and nailbeds. The common mechanism is a general lack of oxygenated hemoglobin being supplied to the tissue. Causes include congenital heart defects that impair perfusion as well as other causes in which perfusion is normal but genetic alterations prevent effective oxygen binding to hemoglobin or there is a decrement in hemoglobin synthesis. With a normal heart and normal perfusion, a hemoglobin-binding alteration is the best fit.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The structurally normal heart with normal perfusion excludes a perfusion-limiting congenital defect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Retained oxygenated hemoglobin describes cyanide poisoning and would appear red, not blue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Complex IV inhibition (cyanide) leaves hemoglobin oxygenated and produces cherry-red rather than blue skin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uncoupling generates heat and does not cause deoxygenated systemic blood.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: Two unknown compounds are tested on cultured cells. Compound X increases oxygen consumption, raises heat output, and does not increase reactive oxygen species. Compound Y decreases oxygen consumption, increases reactive oxygen species, and causes lactate to accumulate. Which of the following pairs best identifies the compounds?

choices.label: A
choices.text: X is 2,4-dinitrophenol; Y is cyanide

choices.label: B
choices.text: X is antimycin A; Y is high-dose aspirin

choices.label: C
choices.text: X is cyanide; Y is uncoupling protein-1

choices.label: D
choices.text: X is oligomycin; Y is uncoupling protein-1

choices.label: E
choices.text: X is rotenone; Y is 2,4-dinitrophenol

explanation.summary: Uncouplers raise oxygen consumption and heat without generating ROS, whereas ETC inhibitors lower oxygen consumption, generate ROS, and drive lactate accumulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uncouplers like DNP allow ETC activity to yield heat instead of ATP; oxygen consumption increases initially, and uncouplers in general do not generate ROS. Inhibitors like cyanide prevent electron flow and oxygen consumption from the start of exposure, are associated with ROS production from inefficient electron transfer, and cause rapid lactate accumulation to rescue ATP production through glycolysis. Compound X therefore behaves as an uncoupler and compound Y as an inhibitor.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Antimycin A is an inhibitor (profile Y), and high-dose aspirin is an uncoupler (profile X).
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cyanide is an inhibitor that decreases oxygen consumption, and UCP-1 is a natural uncoupler that does not produce ROS.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oligomycin inhibits ATP synthase and would not increase oxygen consumption, and UCP-1 is an uncoupler that does not generate ROS.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is reversed; rotenone is a complex I inhibitor (profile Y) and DNP is an uncoupler (profile X).

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A student states that uncoupling protein-1 and 2,4-dinitrophenol both form pores that span the mitochondrial inner membrane. Which of the following best corrects this statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both are freely diffusible chemicals that are not anchored anywhere within the lipid bilayer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both are proteins, but only UCP-1 is anchored within the outer mitochondrial membrane

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neither transports protons across the membrane; both act by inhibiting ATP synthase

choices.label: D
choices.text: UCP-1 is a diffusible chemical not anchored in the bilayer, whereas DNP is a membrane-spanning protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: UCP-1 is a membrane-spanning protein, whereas DNP is a diffusible chemical not anchored in the bilayer

explanation.summary: Natural uncouplers (UCPs) are proteins that span the inner membrane to transport protons, whereas unnatural uncouplers like DNP are freely diffusible chemicals that are not anchored in the lipid bilayer.
explanation.whyCorrect: UCPs are a family of proteins that naturally uncouple OXPHOS for thermogenesis by spanning the mitochondrial inner membrane to transport protons to the matrix apart from ATP synthase. Agents like DNP are chemicals, not proteins; they do not span the membrane but are freely diffusible agents that are not anchored through the lipid bilayer. What the two share is that both produce heat and both decrease ATP production from OXPHOS.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Only DNP is a freely diffusible chemical; UCP-1 is an anchored membrane protein.
whyWrongByChoice.B: DNP is a chemical, not a protein, and UCPs function within the inner (not outer) mitochondrial membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both transport or shuttle protons across the inner membrane; neither acts by inhibiting ATP synthase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the two agents.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview II: OXPHOS Uncouplers and Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is evaluated for fatigue. A complete blood count shows: RBC count 4.5 x10^6/uL (reference 3.8-5.0), hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL (reference 11.9-14.8), hematocrit 32% (reference 35-43), and mean corpuscular volume (MCV) 88 fL (reference 80-96). Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of these results?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Macrocytic anemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Microcytic anemia

choices.label: C
choices.text: No indication of anemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Normocytic anemia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Polycythemia (elevated RBC mass)

explanation.summary: Anemia is defined by a reduction in RBC count, hemoglobin, or hematocrit, and MCV then classifies it.
explanation.whyCorrect: The hemoglobin (10.8) and hematocrit (32%) are both below their reference ranges, which establishes anemia. Because the MCV of 88 fL falls within the reference range, the anemia is classified as normocytic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Macrocytic anemia requires an MCV above the reference range, but this MCV of 88 fL is normal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Microcytic anemia requires an MCV below the reference range, but this MCV of 88 fL is normal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both hemoglobin and hematocrit are below their reference ranges, so anemia is present.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Polycythemia is an increased RBC mass; here the hemoglobin and hematocrit are low, not high.

questions.topicName: Metabolic Overview III: O2 Delivery (1 of 2)

questions.stem: A physiology instructor explains that mature red blood cells maintain ATP for their function strictly through glycolysis and lactate production, even though they carry high concentrations of oxygen. Which feature of the mature red blood cell best accounts for this exclusive reliance on glycolysis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A biconcave disc shape that limits diffusion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absence of mitochondria

choices.label: C
choices.text: An unusually thick, rigid plasma membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insufficient oxygen bound to hemoglobin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Presence of a large nucleus consuming ATP
